# Build: pipeline-rebuild (orchestrator build ID: urgent-rebuild-pipeline-orchestrator-ids-splits-)

## Brett said (verbatim)
You need to start the pipeline over from scratch. From now on, what I say, send a build to the orchestrator. The orchestrator is going to assign an ID. A build ID. He's going to use you to break it up into steps select a model Babel or Opus Babel when it's needed and then he's going to see how many subscriptions are connected to the VPS how many accounts are available How many, what's the max parallel for each one? And uh, if it's a account that has Fable, he'll send the Fable to that. He'll send everything else to Opus. He will, no, he will check the BPS to see what accounts have what slots. Available parallel. Dish out the steps, okay? The steps are marked. We already have the rules for how the steps are marked down into a, in a progress pile and blah blah blah. Updated in real time because you have a monitor watching the progress files. And um, the orchestrator starts starts the head, headless. The orchestrator then sends it to the queue, or he sends it to pending. Yeah, he sends everything to the pending. And I have to send them from pending to queue.

## Addendum (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator doesn't start a headless session right away. If he has slots open, he grabs the next build in the queue and starts the headless session.

## Context found tonight
- The orchestrator (apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator) has NO launch code: nothing in it starts headless sessions. Only deploy/claude-headless.sh enqueues into agent-slots (framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs).
- Pending items are never auto-imported into the orchestrator; 'import' (orchestrator-core.mjs) only copies existing subPrompts, nothing splits.
- HARD RULE in force: no build starts without an orchestrator build ID (launcher enforces it).
- 'Launch builds without asking' (claude-settings) defaults off.
- Profiles were merged into 'all' on Nov 7; queue flagged needsReprocess.

## Do
1. Intake: every new pending item is auto-imported into the orchestrator with a build ID.
2. Split: the orchestrator calls Claude to split into <=30 min steps and pick Fable only where needed, Opus otherwise; write steps to the build.
3. Flow: builds sit in Pending until Brett moves them to Queue (no auto-queue).
4. Dispatcher: a loop in the orchestrator reads VPS accounts (deploy/claude-workers.mjs status, claude-login.mjs accounts): which have Fable, max parallel, free slots. When a slot is free it takes the next Queue build and starts a headless session through the existing launcher (claude-headless.sh / agent-slots), Fable steps to a Fable account, rest to Opus.
5. Progress: steps tick in the progress files per existing rules; the live monitor updates the console in real time.
6. Idle alert: AmberX phone notification when nothing is running while the Queue has work.
7. Tests, report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
When the orchestrator splits a build and sends it to Pending, it also creates a plan in Plan Studio: a note describing the job, with a checklist of the steps, and a sub-note inside it holding Brett's prompt verbatim, with the part this build covers highlighted in a colour set in settings. Sessions are never stopped and rerun per step (saves tokens): instead, the last action of every step is to update the progress file. The orchestrator's listener watches the progress files and, on each change, ticks that step off and crosses it out in the Plan Studio checklist.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator writes each headless session's brief itself, with the least information possible: only the current step(s), the files it touches, and the rules it needs. No history, no full spec.

steps.text: Contract: add the `queued` status to builds@1 / orchestrator@1 / build-hook@1 (Pending → Queued → Building = running), a `pipeline` record on every build (account, session, runs, split, last run) kept across orchestrator writes, pending@1 shows queued as pending, derivedStatus keeps queued; fixtures and check-builds-store updated

pipeline-core.mjs (pure): account capabilities (which account has Fable, max parallel each, limits), the queue order, pick the account for a queued build's next phase, slot-open launch decision, session-end outcome (requeue / back to Pending / failed), idle reasons, the split prompt + step parser (≤30 min, Fable only where needed) and a rules-based fallback split

pipeline.mjs CLI (IO): status | queue | unqueue | split | intake | accounts | tick; store writes under the lock (queue/unqueue/pipeline record/steps from the split); splitter providers (claude -p on a login copy, AXF_PIPELINE_SPLITTER for tests, rules fallback); intake splits every new build with no steps

Dispatcher tick: read VPS accounts + agent slots, when a slot is free take the next Queue build, make its worktree + brief (Brett said block + phase brief), launch deploy/claude-headless.sh --account on a Fable account for Fable phases / Opus otherwise, mark running + account + session; monitor events.jsonl + slots for session end → built / requeue / Pending / failed, relaunch cap; dispatcher state file for the console; cron line in deploy/install-console.sh

Idle alert + notifications: notify.json types (pipeline.idle, pipeline.launched, pipeline.ended, pipeline.failed) raised through the console alerts API from the host (AmberX push for idle: nothing running while the Queue has work, with the reason), keyed and resolved when a build runs

Console: Pipeline tab on the Build orchestrator page (Pending / Queue / Building columns, accounts strip with Fable + parallel + running, dispatcher status, Queue / Back to Pending / Split now, live refresh while visible); server routes GET /pipeline, POST /pipeline/queue | unqueue | split; plugin commands for voice/MCP (queue a build, pipeline status); help entries; Launch builds without asking ON = new builds queue by themselves

Tests: check-pipeline.mjs end to end on a scratch store with a fake launcher, fake splitter and fake accounts (intake → Pending → Queue → launch on the right account → session end → built / requeue / failed, idle alert once, slot cap respected); python route test; CI wiring; plugin-lifecycle check; existing suites green

Close out: report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, _claude/builds/README.md Pipeline section, rules + decisions lines, THREADS row, fold the overlapping builds (idle-alert-phone-flag-when-nothing-is-building, orchestrator-start-a-build-through-the-api-mcp-and-cli) as complete with this PR, commit, push, PR, link the build

# Build: window-resize-fix (Current profile) - URGENT bug fix

## Brett said (verbatim, Nov 3 2026, voice)
"Why can't I resize terminal? All floating windows need to be resizable. And also, I selected dialog for the terminal settings in its settings, but it doesn't open."

Assigned agent: whoever is free (router if on main; else **Landin' Lenny**; record who). Register in the `current` profile (id `window-resize-fix`) + banner entry. Fix right away, tell after.

## Bug 1: floating windows can't be resized (phone at least)
- The window engine got resize from all 8 edges/corners in windows-terminal s6 (refactor-all s17-s23, report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/windows-terminal-fable.md`). Brett can't resize the Terminal floating window now. Find why on the live console (console.amberxai.com, his phone + desktop): handles missing/too small for touch, pointer events not wired for touch (need pointer events + touch-action none on handles), a later change (one-look, xlayout/dock engine #245/#252, compact frame, Molly chrome) overriding the window host, or the Terminal opening in a non-window host.
- Fix in the framework window host so EVERY floating window in every app is resizable: 8 edges + corners, big enough touch targets on phones (invisible hit area ~16-24 px, visible grip in the corner), min/max size from tokens, remembers size per window, double-tap title = maximize/restore. CI test: every floating window exposes resize handles.

## Bug 2: Terminal settings placement 'dialog' does nothing

# Build: terminal-sessions-nav (Current profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): give the Terminal a collapsible navigation menu on the left listing live sessions, including each session he is personally doing with Claude, so he can mirror it and jump in. Assigned agent: whoever is free (router if on main; else **Earl the Ear**; record who). Register in `current` (id `terminal-sessions-nav`) + banner entry. Runs after / builds on `terminal-vps-host` (the Terminal's VPS host must be set up; if that isn't on main yet, wait for it or include its fix).

## Build INTO the existing Terminal plugin (Windows Terminal + headless-tabs). No second terminal.
- s1 **Left nav rail:** collapsible (icon-only collapsed, full when open, swipe/hamburger on phone), framework nav component + tokens, remembers state. Sections: **My sessions** (Brett's own), **Agents** (headless builds, with agent avatar/name, model, live cost, status dot - reuse headless meters), **Connections** (VPS, containers, axHub...). Tap = open/focus that tab; right-click = context menu (open, split, open in Moshi, stop with confirm, session info).
- s2 **My sessions:** (a) Claude Code sessions he runs (tmux / claude-headless / phone via Moshi, Session check-in archive) - live mirror of the tmux pane, read-only by default, **Jump in** = attach writable and type into it. (b) Claude.ai chat/voice sessions (Amber): claude.ai has no live API for the transcript, so mirror what reaches axHub: every axHub call the session makes (tool, args summary, result, approvals) as a live activity feed per session (group by axHub session/correlation + client), with the session's agent (agent-pick) and cost if known; 'Jump in' = open that chat in claude.ai (deep link if the session reports its URL) and keep the feed beside it. Add MCP tool `console_session_note` (allow) so a Claude session can post what it's saying/doing as short lines into its own mirror feed, and add a rule: 'Chat/voice sessions post a short line to console_session_note when they act.' Zero tokens on the console side.
- s3 Session list is live (websocket), shows started time + running timer, sort/search/filter, collapsible groups; ended sessions move to a 'Recent' group (link to Session browser).
- s4 Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI (list sessions, mirror, jump in, stop). Tests, phone + desktop screenshots, UI Review item, report `_claude/builds/reports/terminal-sessions-nav.md`, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.

# Build: profile-manager (Current profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): a plugin to manage build profiles: view, browse, create, edit, delete, everything. Assigned agent: **Landin' Lenny** (book on his card; if busy and the all-rounder router is on main, whoever is free - record who). Register in the **current** profile (id `profile-manager`) + banner entry. (Profile `current` was just created; if it's missing, create it: `node framework/cli/profiles.mjs create "Current" --id current --select`.)

## Build on what exists - don't duplicate
The console already has the **Build profiles** plugin (`build-profiles`: dialog + settings tab, banner chip, switch/create/rename/remove) over `framework/cli/profiles.mjs` (build-profiles@1) and the builds store. Grow THAT plugin into a full manager page (rename the plugin title to 'Build profiles' manager if needed; keep its id, data and every existing feature).

## Features
- **Browse:** framework grid of every profile (collapsible rows): name, id, active star, description, counts (builds running / pending / complete / archived, pending items, queue steps), cost spent + cost left, last activity, created; sort/search/filter. Expand a row: its builds (with agent avatars once crew-live lands), pending list, queue, plan summary, files (`profiles.mjs where`).
- **View** a profile page: all its builds and steps, timeline, totals, links to Builds page views filtered to it.
- **Create** (name, id, description, copy from another profile, catalog on/off, make active), **Edit** (name, description, catalog, colour/icon for the banner chip), **Switch** (one tap; banner chip + context menu), **Duplicate**, **Merge** two profiles, **Move builds** between profiles (multi-select, drag rows onto a profile), **Archive / hide**, **Delete** = take off the list (data kept, restorable) with confirm; a separate 'Delete data too' that is owner-only and irreversible-confirm. Base profile and active profile can't be deleted.
- **Cleanup helper:** flag archived builds that are actually complete (reconciler) - e.g. angel, big-dog, breakroom, refactor - with a one-tap fix.
- Context-menu hooks everywhere: 'Build profiles...' and 'Move to profile' on any build row.
- Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI (list, get, create, update, select, duplicate, merge, move-builds, archive, remove, restore) so Amber can manage profiles by voice (reads ALLOW policy, changes veto, data delete confirm).
- Tests, phone + desktop screenshots, UI Review item, report `_claude/builds/reports/profile-manager.md`, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.

# Build: gizmo-rebuild-fable

## Brett said (verbatim)
"I want to use Fable on the highest possible thinking level on ultra code to rebuild Gizmo." "Go ahead."
Also: "I need more powerful controls over the background listeners for AmberX. I've had problems with the microphone... it's crashing with other apps, and sometimes it'll just do that sound over and over."

Thinking: MAX (AXF_THINKING=max / --effort max). Model Fable for every step.

Rebuild Gizmo (AmberX companion plugin) properly on Fable:
1. Review the existing companion plugin + shared claude-session lib + assistant-chat-mode fast path; keep what is solid, rebuild what isn't. Report what changed and why.
2. Talk mode works with the screen off / app backgrounded (foreground service), transcript in the chat, stop from the notification (replaces the stopped gizmo-voice run; reuse /root/axf-builds/gizmo-voice if it has useful work).
3. Mic / background listener fixes and controls: proper Android audio focus (yield the mic to calls and other apps, resume after), no restart loop replaying the start sound (backoff, max retries, silent restarts), one owner of the mic at a time. Listener control panel in AmberX + console: list every listener, on/off, auto-pause on calls/other apps, sound on/off, retry limits, status and last error, REST/MCP/CLI.
4. Fix the message box sitting under the bottom nav at phone width.
5. Tests, APK via CI, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Tick pending items gizmo-voice and gizmo-companion where covered.

Nothing removed. One session, lean chain. Stay out of notes/tasks, badges and notification-panel code (other builds running).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice)
"I'm thinking maybe we should take Assistant out of AmberX since we just have Gizmo... there's a lot of bloat."
- Move what Gizmo needs from ai-assistant (server chat route, provider, turn router) into the companion plugin / shared claude-session lib.
- Then remove the old Assistant plugin from AmberX (UI, nav, server part, bundle). Gizmo is the only assistant in AmberX. Console's own assistant is not affected unless it only depends on the AmberX copy; check and report.
- Report bundle size before/after.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - overrides Addendum 1's direction
"It should be the other way around. Gizmo should control everything; the assistant should run off of Gizmo."
- Gizmo owns the chat engine: server route, provider, turn router, tools, sessions.
- Any remaining assistant (console assistant, AmberX) becomes a thin client running on Gizmo's engine, no own copy of the logic.
- Remove the duplicated AmberX Assistant bloat once it runs on Gizmo.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice) - the goal
"Gizmo needs to be powerful, hardcore. He's got to be my full Claude client. He's gonna replace the Claude app on my phone. I'm not gonna use the Claude app no more. It's all gonna be Gizmo."
- Target: full Claude app replacement on Brett's phone. Parity list to plan against: voice mode (hands-free, interrupt, screen off), chats with history/search, projects with instructions + files, memory, connectors/MCP (axHub services), web search + fetch, file/photo/camera attach, artifacts/docs, model + thinking picker, timers/alarms/calendar/location on the phone, notifications.
- This run: write the parity plan as a pending item with ~10-min steps (what exists, what's missing, order), build the core (engine ownership, voice screen-off, mic fixes) first, and as much of the rest as fits. Remaining steps stay in the plan for the next run. Don't pad; no extras beyond the list.

## Addendum 4 (Brett, voice)
"I don't really need chat history. I've already got the session logs in AmberX. Don't put that in Gizmo, that'd be dumb."
- Drop chat history/search from the parity list. Gizmo uses AmberX's existing session logs (link to them), no second history store.

## Addendum 5 (Brett, voice) - narrows Addendum 3
"When I say replace Claude on my phone, I mean my interface, my chat, my input interface. Just the chat part."
- Scope = the chat/input experience only: talking and typing to Claude (voice mode hands-free, interrupt, screen off; text input; attachments; streaming replies; tool use through axHub/MCP; model + thinking picker).
- Not in scope: chat history, projects, memory UI, artifacts, phone extras. Drop them from the parity plan.

## Addendum 6 (Brett, voice) - orchestrator-first, no resending
"I don't want you sending everything every time we exchange words. I don't want to resend the whole conversation... Everything I say is gonna go to the orchestrator first. Everything from Gizmo goes through the console. No AI. Until I send it to Claude."
- Gizmo input goes to the console/orchestrator first, plain code, zero tokens. Never resend the whole conversation; send Claude only what's needed.
- Console holds Gizmo input in a sorted, manageable queue (reorder, edit, group/split into threads, delete). Nothing goes to Claude until Brett sends it (one item, a selection, or a thread).
- Settings: Gizmo plugin carries a settings-interface ASSET (every settings interface is an asset) that attaches to the orchestrator's settings interface as its own Gizmo tab (Gizmo-orchestrator integration settings). Gizmo has hooks to open it. Gizmo's existing AmberX settings stay as they are.
- API/MCP/CLI for the queue and settings.

## Addendum 7 (Brett, voice) - searchable transcript database
"I want to be able to search them. I don't want them to be read as memory every time the project loads, but I do want a database created that is searchable."
- Build on PR #365 (ui-review-notify-audio: session recording + transcripts); don't rebuild it.
- One searchable database of every session transcript (full-text, plain code; optional local embeddings later): who, when, session, build, text with timestamps, link to the audio at that moment.
- NEVER loaded into context on project start or by default. Only queried on demand.
- Search tool for Gizmo/Claude (MCP + REST + CLI: transcripts_search, transcript_get) returning short snippets with links; search UI in the console recorder page.

## Addendum 8 (Brett, voice) - make the transcript search full RAG
"Go ahead." (make it a real RAG, search by meaning)
- Install Ollama on the VPS with a small local embedding model (e.g. nomic-embed-text, ~0.5 GB RAM, CPU only). Zero Claude tokens.
- Index every transcript in chunks with embeddings in the background after each session (niced, one at a time); backfill existing transcripts.
- Hybrid search: meaning (vectors) + keywords, ranked; results = short snippets with session, time and audio link.
- Still never auto-loaded into context; only on demand through transcripts_search.

# Build: ui-registry-shortcuts

## Brett said (verbatim)
"Let's go with a UI shortcuts plugin. All the UIs need to be in a registry. Every single dialog, pop-up, settings interface, main plugin screen, every UI element has to be an asset. Every single asset in the whole app and all its plugins, from a button to a pop-up to a link to a menu to a menu entry, every thing needs to be an asset. That needs to be visible to the API." "Create a registry so I can open them with my voice."

1. Audit: list what is already an asset (chrome assets, settings-ui@1, tab-group@1, jump-menu@1, control@1 screens/dialogs, voice-command@1) and what isn't. Report the gap. Reuse existing contracts; don't duplicate control@1 or voice-command@1.
2. One UI registry (framework contract): every screen, dialog, pop-up, settings interface, menu, menu entry, button, link across console, AmberX, Molly, axHub web, and every plugin. Stable id, kind, owner app/plugin, label, aliases, how to open it. Plugins declare theirs; a scanner fills gaps; CI check that new UI is registered.
3. API/MCP/CLI: list, search, get, open/show/trigger any registered item.
4. Voice: UI Shortcuts plugin opens any registered item by voice (aliases, fuzzy match), wired to voice-command@1 and Gizmo; user-defined shortcuts.

"Without AI, I need an assistant that doesn't need Claude, that just knows my app. I should be able to tell it in plain English like: 'yo, make a notification to do this.'"
- Build a local, zero-token assistant on top of the UI registry + voice-command@1 + control@1: plain-English parsing with a grammar/intent matcher (no LLM), fuzzy matching, slots (names, times, on/off), confirmation for writes.
- It can: open any registered UI, change any setting, run any registered command, create/edit notifications and their style (through the notifications plugin's API), queue items for Claude (Gizmo queue) when the request really needs AI.
- Lives on the console; AmberX and Gizmo send it text/voice. 'What can I say?' lists commands. API/MCP/CLI.

"Yes, we're gonna do that." (run a small local model through Ollama)

- Share the Ollama install with the Gizmo rebuild (it installs Ollama + an embedding model for transcript RAG); don't install twice. Setting to turn the model off; memory limit; unload when idle.

A. Badges (one plugin):
1. Claude, axHub, VPS and AmberX badges in ONE plugin; move existing ones in (old ones can be disabled).
2. Per badge: show/hide, icons only or icon + label, label text, icon per state (ok/warn/error/off), banner order.

4. Configurable tap action per badge (drop-down, open screen, run command, toggle, nothing). Usage meter default tap = drop-down of every saved Claude account with credits left, reset times, active marker, status. Plain code, zero tokens, cached + refresh.

B. Notifications panel:
5. Groups (user-made, group on/off), triggers (event, conditions, thresholds, schedule), actions/commands on each notification (approve, open screen, run console command, custom per group). Editable in the panel and via REST/MCP/CLI.

## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - notifications architecture
"Everything's gonna go through the console. It needs to exist on the console, and then that sends the thing to AmberX to do the notification. It doesn't live on AmberX. AmberX just processes commands from the console."
- The notifications engine (registry, rules, groups, triggers, actions) lives on the console only.
- AmberX is a dumb delivery end: it receives notification commands from the console (show, sound, open link, action buttons that call back to the console) and nothing else. No notification logic or rules in AmberX; any that exist there get moved to the console.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
"Can I make it so a notification will be a vibration or an alarm or a certain sound, from the console?"
- Yes: per notification type/group on the console: delivery style = silent / vibrate (pattern) / sound (pick from a list, custom upload) / alarm (full-screen, repeats until dismissed). AmberX executes it (notification channels per style so Android honours it). Test button per type.

"When something is sent over from the console, AmberX opens it up and brings it to the front of my phone. If I say 'open up the console UI Review and bring this project into focus', it brings that right up to the front."
- Console command -> AmberX: bring AmberX to the foreground on the phone (Android full-screen intent / overlay permission as needed) and open the target directly: a screen, a UI Review group, a specific item scrolled into focus.
- New UI Review items auto-open this way (setting to turn off; notification is the fallback).
- Works by voice through the local assistant / Gizmo: 'open UI Review and focus <project>'.

# claude-accounts-edit: Edit button per account that reruns the wizard

(r2: r1 died at launch, account-2 OAuth expired.)

Brett's words (voice, Nov 6 2026): "Where it lists the accounts, I need to have an edit button next to the switch buttons... that runs the wizard again."

## Problem
In the console's Claude accounts list (ai-keys "Manage Claude accounts" view and the claude-accounts screen), each account row only has Switch. When an account's login expires, there is no way to re-log that specific account. The add-account wizard only adds a new one. Also: the wizard's "Save current account" fails with a bare 'VPS command failed, exit 1' when nobody is logged in (claude-account save prints 'nothing to save: log in or pass a token'); show that message in the UI.

## Build
1. Add an **Edit** button on every account row, right next to Switch, in every place the account list is shown.
2. Edit opens the existing add-account wizard bound to that account (pre-filled name/slot). Finishing it replaces that account's login/credentials in place: same slot, no new account. Per-build login copies for that account pick up the new credentials.
3. Show a clear state on rows whose login is expired/invalid (e.g. "Login expired").
4. Wizard: surface the claude-account command's own output on failure instead of only 'exit 1'.
5. Register a console action claude-accounts.edit (account id arg) so it runs through console commands too.

## Rules
Follow CLAUDE.md and _claude/rules/RULES.md. Never print or log secrets/tokens. Tests for the edit path (re-log replaces creds in place, no duplicate). Update help/docs, THREADS row, orchestrator entry, report. Don't land; leave it for Brett's go.

## Brett said (verbatim)
"We need a plugin that will let AmberX open up any website I tell her to."
(Context: amberx.open_url refused www.hostinger.com: "open_url only opens Brett's own sites (amberxai.com)".)

1. amberx.open_url (axHub device service) opens any http/https URL on Brett's paired phone, not only amberxai.com. Block non-http(s) schemes (intent:, file:, javascript:). Audit-log every open.
2. Setting in axHub (owner-only): mode = own sites only / allowlist / any site (default: any site, per Brett). Allowlist editable.
3. AmberX app: opens external sites in the phone's default browser; own sites keep opening in AmberX.
4. Tests, docs (decisions), PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. If the AmberX APK needs a change, note it for an AmberX-AXF follow-up.

One session, lean chain.

origin.said:
"It's gonna be linked to our Gmail through axHub's MCP server, not Claude's. axHub is gonna connect to my Gmail, my Google Calendar, my Google Sheets. axHub needs to connect to my whole Google ecosystem."

1. Google service(s) in axHub: one OAuth sign-in (Brett clicks Connect in axHub web; tokens in the vault, refresh saved on every use). Scopes: Gmail, Calendar, Sheets, Drive, Contacts, Tasks (enable per service).

# Build: notes-tasks-calendar

## Brett said (verbatim)
"In the notes, task manager and to-do (one plugin), we're gonna add a calendar where we can set events and schedules. We can set weekly schedules. And it's gonna be hooked up to our Gmail / Google Calendar through axHub's MCP server."

Base: branch claude/notes-tasks-sync (PR #363, shared notes-tasks plugin); merge it first, build on it.
1. Calendar inside the notes-tasks plugin (console + AmberX): day / week / month / agenda views; events (time, location, notes, reminders); recurring + weekly schedules; tasks with due dates show on it.
2. Two-way sync with Google Calendar through axHub's Google service (build axhub-google, queued). Until that lands, local calendar works on its own; sync switches on when the service exists.
3. Reminders go through the console notifications engine (AmberX only delivers).
4. REST/MCP/CLI + voice commands (UI registry).
5. Tests, README, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly.

One session, lean chain.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice)
"I need a really sweet interface for the scheduling stuff, the schedules. Make it sick."
- Polished, modern calendar UI (framework tokens + theme only): smooth view transitions, drag to create / move / resize events, colour-coded calendars, now-line, mini-month, quick-add bar (plain English: 'gym every Mon Wed 6pm'), weekly schedule editor with drag blocks, phone gestures (swipe days/weeks, long-press drag), dark/light. Phone-first, desktop great too.
- Screenshots of every view (phone + desktop) to UI Review.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
"Open that in its own window with multiple layouts. Open numerous schedules, days and weeks: a week here and a month there, and drag events from here to there. Attach an RSVP list / invite list to an event with a check mark of who's replied. Send automatic emails to RSVP people, or emails asking people to confirm they've read/seen it. It needs to update in the scheduler on AmberX."
- Calendar opens in its own window (windows@1 / dock@1); multiple panes side by side, each any view/date/calendar; save named layouts; drag events between panes.
- Invite / RSVP list per event: guests, status (invited / yes / no / maybe / seen), check marks, counts. Emails sent through axHub Google (Gmail) when it exists: invites, automatic RSVP reminders, read/seen confirmation requests (tracked link). Replies update the event status live on console and AmberX. Sending email = confirm approval (axHub policy).

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
"Any replies to the emails get logged. They type their reply in a text field that's sent in the email; they have to reply in the text field so it gets logged in the system."
- Each invite/reminder email has a link to a small public reply page (per-guest signed token, no login): RSVP buttons + a text field. Submissions are logged on the event (who, when, answer, message) and update status live on console + AmberX.
- Plain email replies are also caught via Gmail (axHub) and logged on the event when possible, but the reply page is the main path.
- Reply page is rate-limited, token expires, no other data exposed.

Opus phase: the host plugin, six standalone add-on plugins, voice + API/MCP/CLI, tests, UI Review. Plan Studio: Proposed > Assets (proposed-fzf3). Supersedes the menu / toolbar editors of the old asset-designer pending build.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

steps.text: designer@1 contract: host + add-on model (designer-addon@1: id, asset types, designer UI view, settings interface asset, designer interface asset, manifest fields, capabilities, drops, voice), the designer asset type (the designer's interface with inherit@1 copies per add-on), rules file + .d.mts, exported from core

Asset output contract: designed@1 manifest + stable identifier (uid, ref, revision, hash, origin), registration as a ui-registry@1 item (coordinated with ui-registry-shortcuts, no duplicate engine) and in the designer library index (designer-library@1, paths per output target); the embed asset type (embed-asset@1)

Interaction contract for every designer (designer-doc@1): one document model with families per asset type (toolbar, banner, nav, app menu, context menu, flat) and asset round trips, ops, multi-select, map canvas (snap, align, distribute, auto layout, zoom), drag-and-drop (parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop), undo / redo with coalescing, the designer context menu + keyboard map

asset-context@1: the context-menu section every UI asset gets (identity with tooltip, live Preview entry, About, Help, Edit in its designer, Copy id, Where used) and assetInfo in every mode (tooltip, hover card, side panel, help text, say); MenuEntry gains tip / preview / disabled; data-axf-asset attribute contract

Fixtures + validators + checks: spec/fixtures/designer.json replayed by spec/check-designer.mjs (CI), both validators agree, starters (designer ×7, settings ×7, embed ×3), JSON Schemas, re-bake + shared-assets bake, PORTING.md row, DESIGNER.md spec, report, Opus steps written into the plan
PR into the merge queue (never landed directly), THREADS.md + STATUS.md + decisions.md, build linked (builds-live.mjs link)

builds.title: Icon Browser plugin + Icon Manager (icon library, icon maps, icon packs)
builds.detail: Icon Browser plugin: starter library of open-licensed icon sets stored as icon-pack assets (framework/icon-library, served by the plugin, never bundled); tree / grid / list views with categories, sort, filter, search and a thumbnails toggle; configurable sources of any kind (local, HTTP, REST, MCP, FTP/SFTP, Google Drive, Google Photos, Dropbox, known online repositories) with per-type forms and secrets in the plugin's private store; packs composed by drag and drop between collapsible / floatable panes; selected icons open into docked or floating tab groups; packs saved as icon-pack assets. Icon Manager: every UI and plugin has an icon map (icon-map@1: slot -> icon ref, inheritance app root -> UI -> plugin, child overrides parent); list / grid of every UI with a map, filterable by app; map editor + live preview with drops; Save / Apply; a global pack listing every icon; switch packs globally, randomize, generate cohesive packs. Everything is assets with API / MCP / CLI parity and voice actions; settings in categorized collapsible sections; UI options to UI Review first (3+).

# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

origin.brief:
# Model UPGRADES need Brett's approval; downgrades don't (Urgent, Opus)

Replaces the stopped build model-switch-approval (folder /root/axf-builds/model-switch-approval, ignore any work there).

Brett Nov 3 2026 (voice), angry: a headless build (agent-swarm-fable-rebuild, PR #247) approved its own Opus -> Fable phase switch in the orchestrator (`orchestrator.mjs act approve`) because its brief said "do every step". Brett: "It cannot be switching the model without my approval. That's not even a veto. That's an approval." Then: "You can downgrade, but you can't upgrade."

New project rule (add to _claude/rules/RULES.md and the decisions log, dated Nov 3 2026): a build may switch to a LOWER model on its own (downgrade, e.g. Fable -> Opus): allowed, no approval, just recorded. Switching to a HIGHER model (upgrade, e.g. Opus -> Fable) needs Brett's explicit APPROVAL (confirm policy), never a veto countdown and never self-approved by a session, agent, headless build or the orchestrator. Ranking: Fable is above Opus (Brett's call). Put the ranking in model-policy (one ordered list, config not code) so future models slot in. A session that reaches an upgrade stops there and asks.

Enforce it:
1. orchestrator approve/phase logic (orchestrator-core.mjs apply + CLI + console server): a downgrade phase passes by itself (record it); an upgrade phase refuses unless approved by Brett: his own signed-in console click or an axHub approval he approves. Detect non-human sources with the same signals used for 'who asked' on approvals (X-Axhub-Source, AXF headless env, agent env). Record who approved and when.
2. vps.build_start / claude-headless.sh / agent job router: launching or relaunching a build on a higher model than its orchestrator step's model is an upgrade too: refuse or hold for approval the same way.
3. Briefs (orchestrator `brief`, headless guidance, agent jobs): say plainly upgrades need Brett and the session stops and asks; downgrades are fine. Remove any wording that lets a session approve an upgrade.
4. Request path: an axHub approval (confirm policy, not veto) titled with the build, the phase and from -> to model; approving it records the approval in the orchestrator.
5. Audit: list every upgrade approved so far by a non-human source (the store's journal), report in the PR; mark agent-swarm-fable-rebuild's s7 Opus -> Fable as self-approved (not Brett's). Note: xlayout-opus and token-control-opus were Fable -> Opus (downgrades), fine under the new rule.
6. Tests for refusal, downgrade pass-through and the approval path; THREADS row (profile urgent); PR (push banner merges it).

Rules: one session, no sub-agents, stay on Opus. Don't approve any phase yourself while doing this.

Requested by Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice). GO given. Build it now, start to finish.

## Problem
The Build orchestrator on main is stale. `_claude/builds/profiles/*/orchestrator.json` is a read-only export of `_claude/builds/store.json`, regenerated after every store write. Banners and THREADS are wrong as a result.

- s7 Tests (store write retry, parallel writes, merge no-regress, reconciler matching), full local CI block, report `_claude/builds/reports/orch-live-sync.md`, THREADS.md, open the PR.

Mark each step done through the store as you finish it (that write itself should go live once s1 exists). Code, comments and commits stay clean and professional.

  - `_claude/builds/store.json` + journal: merge per record by `rev`/updatedAt, newest wins, never drop a record from either side. Orchestrator/pending/queue exports: regenerate from the merged store (never pick a side).

## What Brett wants
1. Every terminal tab in the console's terminal (the Windows Terminal plugin / terminal in the console) runs on a session that never dies, like Mosh/Moshi: it survives disconnects, reloads, phone sleep, and stays current. Browsers can't speak Mosh (UDP), so: every tab is backed by a persistent tmux session on the VPS, attached over the console's websocket/pty bridge with automatic reconnect + resume (scrollback replay on reattach, no lost output). The same tmux sessions must be attachable from Brett's Moshi phone app (document the one-line `mosh`/ssh + `tmux attach -t <name>` command in the help pack and show it in a tab menu item "Open in Moshi" that copies it). Closing a tab detaches, it doesn't kill (explicit "Kill session" with confirm).
2. Every time a headless session starts (deploy/claude-headless.sh, `vps.build_start`, agent swarm jobs, orchestrator-launched builds), the console automatically opens a NEW tab attached to that build's tmux session (axf-<name>). Works for builds started while the console is closed too: on open, tabs for all running headless sessions appear.
3. Tab title bar: the agent running it (agent/persona name from the session's env/brief/swarm roster, e.g. the swarm agent name, else the build name) + model + a real-time cost counter that climbs as it spends. Cost: run claude -p with `--output-format stream-json --verbose` (or tee it alongside the human log) and sum usage per message (input, output, cache read, cache write) x the model's price table (config file, not hard-coded in UI); final value reconciles to the result event's total_cost_usd. Expose cost via a small server route/websocket so the title updates live. Show status dot (working / waiting / done / failed).
4. The tab splits into two panes; split direction vertical or horizontal (toggle in the tab menu + default in Settings, remembered per tab). Pane A = the live session. Pane B = the context chain: as the session reads CLAUDE.md and every file it pulls in (imports/@ references, .claude/rules, _claude/rules/RULES.md, shared rules, instructions, persona, memory, THREADS etc.), show the chain as a tree in the order it happens, and print the rules it picks up ONE AT A TIME, deliberately slower than real time (typewriter/reveal pacing, speed setting, skip-to-end button), so Brett can watch what the agent is learning. Source the chain from the session's actual reads (stream-json tool events for Read, plus the CLAUDE.md load order Claude Code uses); rules = the bullet/heading items of each file.
5. Tokens only, follows the hub look, phone-friendly (on narrow screens the split stacks and becomes swipeable).

Extend that plugin; do NOT create a separate terminal plugin or a second terminal UI. Persistent tmux sessions become the Terminal's session backend / a connection type, auto-opened headless tabs are Terminal tabs, title/cost/status live in its tab strip, the split + context-chain pane are Terminal pane features. # Job: land-everything (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): "Fuck the review, I review it. Just go. Get everything live." He is away; land the finished work on main and get it deployed. He explicitly waived UI Review for these (EXCEPT banners, see below).

## First
- Register in the Urgent profile via the orchestrator CLI (id `land-everything`) + banner entry. orch-live-sync is on main (live status writes, reconciler, claude-sync auto-resolve rules): use its tools for every store write and conflict.
- Check the `land` job type (`node framework/cli/agent-job.mjs list`); if an agent owns landing, you are acting for it this once at Brett's request; book it there if the tooling allows.

## How to land each one
For each branch below, in this order: fetch, merge origin/main into the branch in its worktree (/root/axf-builds/<name> where it exists, else a fresh worktree), resolve, run the repo's local CI block (tsc, vite builds of affected apps, check-theme, check-controls, plugin lifecycle, tests touched), push the branch, then fast-forward/merge to main and push main (never force). Close the PR as merged (or merge it via GitHub API) and update its build in the store (complete, per-step branch/pr/merged/mergedAt).
Conflict rules:
- `_claude/builds/store.json`: merge per record (build, step) by rev/updatedAt, newest wins, never drop a record from either side; then regenerate all exports (`orchestrator.json`, profiles/*/orchestrator.json, pending, queue) from the merged store. Journal `_claude/builds/journal/*.jsonl`: union of lines, dedupe identical, keep chronological order.
- THREADS.md, STATUS.md, decisions.md, LOG.md, notes/sessions/handoffs: union merge. Build reports: keep the branch's version (it's that build's own report) unless main's is newer for the same build.
- Hub-synced copies (changes/*.json, _claude/shared/notes/**, apps/*/_claude/**): identical = fine; differing = newer wins.
- REAL code conflicts: resolve them properly if the intent of both sides is clear (both features must keep working; run the tests). If you can't resolve one safely, skip that branch, leave it pushed, and record exactly why in the report; keep going with the rest.

## Order
1. claude/notes-vault (PR #256)
2. claude/agent-chats-hub (PR #248) - Brett wants this one live ASAP (Breakroom group chat viewer)
3. claude/kill-patches-pilot (AmberX PR; its axHub PR too, in /root/axHub or a fresh clone)

8. claude/theme-editor (PR #243), claude/one-look-default-2 (PR #244), claude/model-upgrade-approval (PR #253)

When they finish (check `vps` builds / tmux axf-theme-veto-pass, axf-plugin-commands-auto): claude/theme-veto-pass (after #250) and claude/plugin-commands-auto (after #250, #249, #256); and the axHub repo branch claude/axhub-veto-pass. Wait for them if they're still running (poll every few minutes, up to 3 hours).
DO NOT land: claude/banner-pack (#251), claude/banner-editor (#254), claude/banners-one (Brett wants to review banners himself). Leave them untouched.

## After landing
- Make sure deploys ran (deploy workflow / Coolify) and the console, axHub web, AmberX web and Molly are up and healthy (docker ps, HTTP 200 on their domains).
- Register the console's MCP (`axf-console` and token-control's MCP) as axHub services if not already (`~/hub/bin/axhub services ...` per axHub examples/README.md), policy preset: reads allow, writes veto, deletes confirm (use the preset from axhub-veto-pass if landed).

# Build: menu-scroll (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): "The application menus need to be scrollable when they reach beyond the screen." Assigned agent: **Janitor Joey** (book on his agent-swarm card; set AXF_AGENT=janitor-joey if supported, else record in report + store note). Register in Urgent (id `menu-scroll`) + banner entry.

## Fix (framework level, so every app and plugin gets it)
- Application menu bar dropdowns, their submenus, and also context menus / overflow (⋯) menus: when a menu is taller than the space left in the viewport, cap its height to the available space (respect safe-area insets, the banner/toolbars, and the on-screen keyboard; use visualViewport on mobile) and make it scroll vertically inside.
- Smooth touch scrolling on phones (overscroll contained so the page behind doesn't scroll), wheel + keyboard arrow navigation scrolls the highlighted item into view, subtle top/bottom fade or chevron hints when there's more.
- Positioning: flip up / shift to stay on screen before falling back to scroll; submenus that would go off the right edge open to the left; on compact width they stay inside the screen.
- Max height + hint style come from tokens/assets (menu asset or component-sizing), no hard-coded sizes (check-theme must pass).
- Apply in the framework menu components (web reference + axf.css) so console, axHub web, AmberX (Capacitor) and every plugin inherit it; Compose twin recorded in PORTING.md unless trivial.
- Tests (overflow cases: long menu at bottom of a short phone screen, nested submenu at the edge, keyboard open), before/after screenshots at 412 px and 1280 px, UI Review item, report `_claude/builds/reports/menu-scroll.md`, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.

# Build: toolbar-tap-confirm (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): every EXISTING and FUTURE toolbar uses the Terminal's Tooltip mode (first tap shows what the button does and arms it lit for 3 s, second tap within 3 s runs it, duration configurable; built in headless-tabs PR #259, s8). The double tap is ONLY on phones / touch. On a computer it stays a normal single click (hover tooltip as usual) - 'it really works on a computer.' Assigned agent: **Landin' Lenny** (book on his card; AXF_AGENT=landin-lenny if supported). Register in Urgent (id `toolbar-tap-confirm`) + banner entry.

## Steps
- s1 Lift Tooltip mode out of the Terminal plugin into the framework toolbar component (web reference + axf.css; Compose twin in PORTING.md unless trivial) as one shared behaviour; the Terminal uses the framework version (no duplicate code left in the plugin).
- s2 Device rule: double-tap confirm only when the input is touch (pointer: coarse / touch events / compact window class on a touch device). Mouse/trackpad/pen-hover = single click + hover tooltip. Decide per interaction (a touchscreen laptop: touch = double tap, mouse = single click).
- s3 Adopt everywhere: every toolbar in the console, every plugin, axHub web, AmberX (Capacitor), Molly, walkthrough-studio, templates/boilerplates, so new apps get it by default. Inventory every toolbar first and list them in the report.
- s4 Future-proof: the framework toolbar has it ON by default; a check (like check-controls) fails CI if any toolbar is built outside the framework toolbar or turns the behaviour off without an explicit, recorded reason. Add the rule to shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'Every toolbar uses tap-to-confirm on touch (framework toolbar); single click on desktop.'
- s5 Settings > Appearance (or Interaction): on/off for touch, arm duration (default 3 s); per-toolbar override only via the setting, not code. Destructive buttons keep their own confirm on top.
- s6 Tests (touch vs mouse paths, timeout, second tap on a different button re-arms instead of running), screenshots phone + desktop, UI Review item, report `_claude/builds/reports/toolbar-tap-confirm.md`, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice, before start): make all of this ONE Toolbars plugin
The framework toolbar becomes a **Toolbars plugin** (plugin@1, lifecycle install/uninstall) that owns every toolbar in every app, existing and future. Everything below is part of it.

### Settings
- Plugin settings (Settings > Plugins > Toolbars): global on/off for the touch double-tap tip (default on, phone/touch only), arm duration, defaults for all toolbars (theme, colours, density, icon size, labels on/off, position).
- **Every toolbar carries its OWN settings** (stored per toolbar id, synced via axHub like other settings): theming and colours (tokens/assets only: colour theme, style, background, button style, icon/label size, spacing, rounded/flat, opacity), layout (position, orientation, wrap vs scroll vs overflow menu, show/hide, auto-hide), behaviour (double-tap override for this toolbar, tooltips), and its button list.
- **Context-menu hooks on every toolbar** (right-click / long-press): 'Toolbar settings' (that toolbar's own settings), 'Edit toolbar' (opens the Toolbar editor), 'All toolbars...' (Toolbars plugin page that lists and controls every toolbar in the app). Contributed as runtime context items, so every existing and future toolbar gets them; CI check fails any toolbar without them.

### Toolbar editor
- Opens from the toolbar context menu. Add / remove / reorder / group / separators, edit each button (label, icon, tooltip text, action/hook, colour, visibility by level/role, keyboard shortcut), reset to default, undo/redo, live preview, save as an asset so it's hot-swappable and shareable.

### Drag and drop hooks anywhere
- A **hook** = any actionable thing in the app (menu item, nav item, toolbar button, banner item, 'Go to it' hooks, plugin commands from control@1 / plugin-commands-auto, settings pages, screens). Reuse the control@1 command registry and the pending `context-menu-editor` idea (save the action/destination, not the element).
- Drag any hook from anywhere and drop it on a **drop target**: any toolbar, the navigation menu, the banners, application menus, context menus, Home. Drag a button from one toolbar to another; nav menu -> toolbar and toolbar -> nav menu.
- On drop: a **configure dialog that depends on where it's dropped** (toolbar = new button dialog; nav menu = nav item dialog; banner = banner item dialog; menu = menu item dialog), prefilled with default values from the hook (label, icon, action, tooltip), with all the options for that target. Confirm creates it; move vs copy choice (default: copy from menus, move between toolbars), undo.
- Make it a framework contract: `drop-target@1` (what it accepts + which configure dialog) and `hook@1` (draggable action descriptor), open registries so any plugin/app can add targets and hooks without kernel changes. Phone: long-press to pick up, drag with edge auto-scroll, drop zones highlight.
- **Banners:** only add the banner drop target through the generic contract. Do NOT merge or rewrite banner-pack (#251), banner-editor (#254) or banners-one work; Brett is reviewing those himself. Note any overlap in the report.
- Rules: add to shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'Every toolbar is a Toolbars plugin toolbar: per-toolbar settings + editor via its context menu, tap-to-confirm on touch only, accepts dropped hooks.' Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI.
- Split into clear steps in the store; tests for drop targets/dialogs/move-copy/undo, phone + desktop screenshots, UI Review items.

# Build: claude-settings (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): "I need a plugin called Claude. Claude settings. A setting to enable your no-wait in that. A whole bunch of settings that are for Claude, that you check on axHub and then act accordingly." Assigned agent: **Janitor Joey** (book on his card; AXF_AGENT=janitor-joey if supported). Register in Urgent (id `claude-settings`) + banner entry.

## Plugin
Console plugin **Claude** (plugin@1, lifecycle install/uninstall, page + Settings > Plugins > Claude, context-menu hook 'Claude settings' everywhere). Settings are stored on axHub (shared `_data/claude/settings.json` or a hub settings namespace) so every Claude session (voice, chat, Claude Code, headless agents) reads the same values.

## Settings (grouped, framework settings renderer with the level toolbar)
- **No wait** (owner-only): when ON, Amber's held calls run immediately instead of the 90 s veto / approval. Implement as a standing axHub pass that the console creates on Brett's signed-in click (reuse pass-all / `axhub.pass_grant` machinery, scope all, `include_irreversible` false by default with its own separate switch 'Include irreversible' also owner-only). Options: duration (1 h / 4 h / until I turn it off), auto-off at night. Banner chip while on. Turning it off revokes the pass instantly.
- **Follow Amber** (link to / share state with the follow-amber build's switch; don't duplicate it - read the same setting).
- **Builds:** default model (Opus/Fable/split), launch builds without asking (on/off), max parallel builds, per-build budget cap and daily budget cap (stop + notify when hit), always assign a named agent (locked on), UI Review gate (on).
- **Verification:** trust live store by default, verify only on conflict (current rule) vs always verify.
- **Talking:** persona on/off, tone level, address terms, swearing level, response length (short/normal/detailed), say costs out loud, read build reports aloud vs summary.
- **Notifications:** push on build done / blocked / approval waiting, quiet hours.
- **Memory/notes:** save session notes to Notes Vault automatically, handoff note at end of session.
- Open registry so new Claude settings can be added as data without code changes.

## Claude reads them
- MCP tools via axf-console (and axHub builtin if simpler): `claude_settings_get` (policy ALLOW, read-only) returning all values with plain descriptions; `claude_settings_set` for NON-owner settings only (veto policy). Owner-only settings (No wait, Include irreversible, approvals, budget caps raising) can ONLY be changed by Brett's signed-in console click - agents/sessions can never change them (test enforces).
- Rule in shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md (top): 'At session start and before acting, read Claude settings (claude_settings_get) and follow them.'
- Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI.

## Done

# Build: smart-menus (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): "I need a dynamic context menu that draws itself depending on where it is and what it's doing. Most common / most likely things at the top. It learns and remembers, predicts what I'm most likely gonna want, keeps that at the top." Assigned agent: **Earl the Ear** (book on his card; if busy and the all-rounder router is on main, whoever is free - record who). Register in Urgent (id `smart-menus`) + banner entry.

## Build (framework level: every context menu in every app, existing and future)
- s1 **Context-aware drawing:** the context menu engine builds the menu at open time from: the target under the pointer (element kind, hook@1 / control@1 target, plugin, screen), its state (selected, running, failed, waiting on approval, has PR, etc.), the current screen, device (phone/desktop). Plugins contribute items with `when` conditions (state predicates) so irrelevant items never show; runtime context items stay the contribution path.
- s2 **Learning ranking, zero tokens:** record every pick locally + synced to axHub per user: (context key = target kind + state + screen, item id, time). Rank with frecency (frequency x recency decay) per context, plus time-of-day and 'what I just did' sequence boosts (simple Markov next-action counts). Top section 'Suggested' = top 3-5 predicted items; the rest grouped below in stable order so muscle memory still works. Plain code, NO LLM calls (test fails if the engine imports an LLM client).
- s3 Pinned items always first (from the pending `context-menu-editor` idea: user pins), then Suggested, then the rest; destructive items never auto-promoted to the top.
- s4 Settings (Settings > Menus, and a 'Menu settings' hook in every context menu): learning on/off, number of suggestions, reset learning (per menu / all), show why it's suggested (tiny hint), privacy: data stays on his axHub.
- s5 Works with menu-scroll (#268) placement and the toolbar build's hook@1/drop-target@1 if on main (don't edit their files). Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI (get suggestions, reset, pin).
- s6 Tests (ranking math, context keys, when-conditions, reset, destructive never top), phone + desktop screenshots, UI Review item, report `_claude/builds/reports/smart-menus.md`, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice, before start): dynamic SECTIONS, not the whole menu
Don't make the whole menu dynamic. Each context menu keeps its normal fixed items in their fixed order (muscle memory). Add dynamic SECTIONS on top of that:
- A 'Suggested' section at the top (learned/predicted items, 3-5, per s2) - can be turned off.
- A context section (items that only apply to this target/state, per s1 'when' conditions), clearly grouped.
- Pinned items (user pins).
The rest of the menu is static and never reorders. A menu asset declares which dynamic sections it shows and where; the default is Suggested at top + context section, static items below.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice): application menus too + 'what we're talking about' goes to the top
- The dynamic sections apply to the **application menu bar** too (every top-level menu: Builds, View, Tools, etc.), not just context menus. Permanent items stay fixed; each menu can declare dynamic sections.
- New dynamic section **'Talking about'** at the top of every menu (app menus + context menus): items relevant to what Brett and Amber (Claude) are currently talking about. Example: open Builds in the app menu while we're discussing the toolbar build -> that build (open it, its PR, its UI Review, its agent, stop it) is at the top.
- How it knows: add MCP tool `console_context` (policy ALLOW, navigation-only, no data change) on axf-console: {topics: [{kind: build|plugin|screen|pr|agent|setting|profile|note, id, label}], ttl_min?}. Amber calls it whenever the conversation moves to something (and console_show / follow-amber can feed it too). The console keeps a short rolling 'current topics' list per user (decays after ~30 min or when replaced), synced live to every open console client.
- Each menu maps topics to its relevant actions via plugins' contributed items with `when` conditions + the control@1 command registry (e.g. a build topic -> Builds menu shows Open build / Open PR / Open UI Review / Agent / Stop). Plain code, zero tokens.
- Settings > Menus: 'Talking about' section on/off, how long topics stay.
- Rule in shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'When the conversation moves to something in the console, call console_context with it.'

## Addendum 3 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice): all of it lives in ONE Menus plugin with tons of customization
- Everything in this build (dynamic sections in app menus + context menus, Suggested, Talking about, context section, pins, learning) is controlled by a **Menus plugin** (plugin@1, lifecycle install/uninstall, page + Settings > Plugins > Menus + a 'Menu settings' hook in every menu's context menu). Removing the plugin falls back to plain static menus.
- **Customization (tokens/assets only, saved per user on axHub, live preview, presets, reset, export/import as a menu-style asset):**
  - Colours: menu background, text, hover/selected, section headers, separators, icons, per-section accent (Suggested / Talking about / Pinned / context), badge colours, shadow, border, blur/glass, opacity.
  - Fonts: family, size, weight, letter spacing, section header style, icon size, density/row height, padding, corner radius, width min/max.
  - Animations: open/close (fade, scale, slide, drop, none), duration + easing, submenu reveal, item stagger, hover effect, highlight pulse for 'Talking about' items, reduced-motion respected.
  - Sections: order, on/off, max items each, labels, icons, collapse/expand, show 'why suggested' hint.
  - Behaviour: learning on/off + reset, topic lifetime, open on hover vs click (desktop), long-press time (phone), keyboard shortcuts.
  - Per-menu overrides (each app menu / context menu can have its own look and sections) from the hook in that menu.
- Works with menu-scroll (#268) placement and the Toolbars plugin (toolbar-tap-confirm build) through framework APIs - don't edit their files; share the hook@1 / drop-target@1 contract if it's on main.
- Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI (get/set menu settings, presets, reset learning, topics).

steps.text: card@1 asset type in framework/schemas/asset-types.json (+ axf schemas): id, owner (plugin id or "console"), title, icon, kind (stat | list | meter | chart | feed | status | actions | custom), size (s | m | l | wide | tall), data {service (plugin_services capability), path, refreshSec, live:boolean}, slots (headline, value, sub, rows, sparkline, actions), emptyState, actions (ids run through the action engine), level (Simple/Basic/Developer/Administrator), minRole (UAC), defaultVisible, order, category. Open registry: unknown kinds render the custom slot, never fail.

plugin@1 gets `cards: ["cards/<id>.json", …]` (card assets ship inside the plugin folder, so plugin-lifecycle@1 removes them on uninstall); plugin-inventory@1 engine lists each plugin's cards (framework/core/engines/plugins.ts + server/engine.py twin) so anything can detect them; future card SDK attaches cards to a plugin by writing this list.

home-cards@1 engine (TS reference, framework/core/engines/cards.ts): collects every card from enabled plugins + console-owned cards, applies saved visibility/order/size, level and role; hidden cards stay in the output with `hidden: true` so Home ALWAYS renders (mounts) every card and only hides it (instant show, data kept warm). Fixture spec/fixtures/home-cards.json; Kotlin twin recorded as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android on hold).

card-layout@1 asset type: columns per window class (compact/medium/expanded), gap + density tokens, grouping (none | plugin | category), "show all / hide all" default, sort (manual | category | plugin). 3 starter layouts: grid-auto, two-column-dashboard, compact-list. Hot-swap via runtime.swap('card-layout', id); tokens only (THEMING.md).

Placeholders for the future card SDK: `axf.cards@1` capability service (list/register/unregister cards at runtime), extension point `home.cards`, typed NotImplemented card designer entry, so a designer plugin can later author card assets and attach them to any plugin without kernel changes.

builds.title: PR browser + Batch Manager
builds.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Grid of push batches with live badges, Merge/Hold on rows, expandable PR sub-grid, failing check + Fix. Dense: small type, small badges, no clutter. Left click opens review, right click menu. PR BROWSER (Brett, Oct 31): a tab listing every open PR across AmberX-AXF, axHub and Build-Pilot. One dense line per PR with everything: number, title, branch, built by (agent/session), live checks badge, behind main, mergeable/conflict, in which batch, age, cost. Expand a row: every check with its error lines, files changed, commits, description, linked build/plan, and actions: Fix, Merge (via batch), Add to batch, Close. Sort/search/filter like every grid; live updates. ROW LEAD (Brett): every row starts with the PR number + a plain-English line of what it does (e.g. '#187 Audio Extract: pulls audio out of screen recordings, no mic'), written from the actual diff not just the title; badges follow on the same line. SCREENSHOTS (Brett): every PR gets BEFORE (main) and AFTER (PR branch) screenshots of the screens it touches, captured automatically by CI/headless browser (web) and emulator (Android); small before/after thumbnails on the row, side-by-side or slider compare in the expanded view, stored with the PR. SCREENSHOT CORRECTION (Brett): do NOT build a new capture system - REUSE the existing pre-build and post-build screenshots the framework already takes (find them first). BEFORE = the existing pre-build screenshot. AFTER: if the PR/build is not done yet, show a PREDICTED screenshot (rendered mockup of the expected result from the build spec + diff so far, clearly badged 'Predicted'); as soon as the build finishes, the real post-build screenshot replaces it automatically (badge 'Real'), live, no refresh. FEATURE SHOTS (Brett): the existing pre/post-build screenshots are NOT enough - they must show the ACTUAL FEATURE the PR built. Per PR, build a feature map from the diff (changed plugins, components, routes, menus, dialogs -> the screens and states that show them). Drive the existing capture tooling to navigate to each one, open it (expand the row, open the dialog/menu, switch the tab, put it in the right state with demo data), and shoot it: BEFORE on main, AFTER on the PR branch. Each shot cropped to the feature plus a full-screen version, web + Android. Brand-new UI has no before: show a 'New' card. Every feature shot shows Predicted (mockup from spec + diff) until the build is done, then the real shot replaces it live. Captions say which feature each shot is. Missed features (no shot) flagged on the row.

builds.title: Framework grid: built-in sort, search, filter + Date and time column
builds.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Every grid that lists builds, tasks, asks or anything else is sortable, searchable and filterable, taking little screen. Basic filter attached by default. Tap header sorts, tap again reverses, long-press adds a second sort. One thin row: small search box + filter icon; on phones just a search icon. Filters hidden until used, then small clearable chips. Custom tables move onto the framework grid. Android parity. Per grid: right-click a grid or its header -> Filter -> off/on for this grid; 'All grids...' lists every grid in the app with the right-clicked one scrolled into view and highlighted, a switch per grid; a default switch decides whether new grids get the filter (on). Defaults are decided per grid by the build: on for data grids with many rows or columns (builds, asks, changes, plugins, PRs), off for small lists (settings, keys, short pickers); record the choice and reason per grid. On grids where it is off, hovering the header for a moment shows a tooltip 'Add the filter to this grid?' with Enable (long-press on phones). Framework grid (part of the app, not the filter plugin): every grid that has no date/time column gets an automatic 'Date and time' column (row created / last changed), hidden by default; grids that already show a date/time get nothing. Right-click the header -> Show/Hide 'Date and time'. Web + Android. UPDATE (Brett): build BOTH into the framework grid. Sort/search/filter live in the framework (not the Basic filter plugin); smart per-grid defaults, right-click on/off, All grids list and hover offer all framework features. Date and time column is ensured at first render: if a grid renders without one, the framework adds the hidden column then. New grids get everything automatically. CI check flags any table not built on the framework grid.

builds.title: Agent swarm: headless specialist agents, conflict-free, token-cheap
builds.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Brett's own agents aren't programmed well; Claude designs as many specialist agents as needed with specific skills. The build orchestrator splits each build into jobs and dispatches them to agents so many builds run at once without stepping on each other. Each agent runs its own headless Claude Code run with ONLY what the job needs: the task, the exact leased files, and the few relevant snippets the orchestrator pre-extracts (no CLAUDE.md dump, no repo exploring). Token efficiency is a hard requirement (sub-agents cost a fortune): cheapest capable model per job (small model for docs/manifests/renames, Sonnet/Opus for code, Fable only for design/contract work); max turns and token budget per run, killed when over; only the tools the job needs; shared skill prefix first so prompt caching applies; short structured JSON report back. No conflicts: file leases per job, overlapping jobs sequenced, shared files (notes, registries, catalogs, tracker) written only by the orchestrator after merge, pre-push lease check, batch merge. Cost meter: tokens and dollars per agent, job and build, visible in the orchestrator. Persona: every agent has Amber's persona (blunt street slang, heavy cussing, wild, still honest about builds), as the full few-line Amber persona (Brett: it's like five lines) in the cached shared prefix. It applies to reports and anything said to Brett; code, code comments and commit messages stay clean and professional. Agent statuses (set from a dropdown on each agent's row in the Agent manager, with a note): On duty (gets work), Off duty (skipped, keeps everything), Injured (keeps failing; no new jobs, flagged for a fix), Medical leave (benched until a date, then back on duty automatically), Probation (small jobs only, Brett notified every run), Fired (never assigned again, kept greyed in history), Custom (Brett names it and picks whether it gets work). The orchestrator only dispatches to agents whose status allows it. Spend per agent on its row: dollars and tokens all time, this week, today, average per job; optional spend cap that auto-benches the agent when hit. Sortable by cost. Status and spend also shown in the session browser. CARDS (Agent manager): one card per agent with photo avatar (unique look per agent), name, role, specialty on its own line, status badge, hiring date, spend (all time, week, today), jobs done, success rate, failures, avg cost per job, favorite model, last seen, Amber-style catchphrase; tap for profile: bio, skills, spend cap, status history, feed of latest runs with cost (opens the session browser). Social profiles live inside the system only, no real social media accounts. GROUP CHAT: a chat window like a normal conversation, switch to enable/disable for all agents plus per-agent; main room plus each agent's history on its profile. Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): make a plugin with a toolbar of programmable actions for filtering, sorting and searching grids. Toolbar name: Share Search. HELD: Brett said 'send to orchestrator and hold off on build' — don't start until he says.

builds.title: Approval history with costs: every approval recorded with details + cost, browsable in Console + axHub
builds.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): 'Add cost of approval every time something is approved and display costs, as well as all details and history of past approvals browsing. Can you alert when needing approval without stopping and restarting.' Context: he asked whether sending an approval and waiting costs tokens. Answer given: waiting is free, but each retry check re-reads the conversation (mostly cached). The 15 s x10 then 1 min rule costs about 10-15 checks per 5 minutes. HELD: queued, not started. Picks (cards): profile Refactor, held; history in the Console AND on axHub's approvals page.

Scope:
1) Cost per approval: every approval records the session's token/cost spent while it waited (number of checks, tokens in/out, cached vs not, USD from framework/schemas/model-pricing.json), plus the time it waited and who/what asked (session, surface, machine, build ref, reason title/description, exact call, result).
2) History browser: every past approval with all details and its cost; filter/sort/search, totals per day/build/session. Console = History view in the approvals-banner plugin (framework DataGrid, expanding rows). axHub = same list on its approvals page. Approve stays on the first screen.
3) Alert without stopping/restarting: a hub-side wait (axhub tool, e.g. approvals.wait / long-poll on the confirmation id, up to ~10 min per call) so a session makes ONE call that returns the moment Brett approves. No retry loop and no session restart. The AmberX app push (already shipped, amberx-push) fires when the approval is created. Then update the shared retry rule (15 s x10, then 1 min) to 'one wait call, re-issued only if it times out' — Brett to confirm that rule change at build time.
Work spans MossesX/axHub (wait tool, cost fields, approvals page history) and AXF (approvals-banner History view, cost capture via codebase-changes hooks / session transcript).

Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): "Add those plus build a powerful terminal plugin that looks and feels and behaves exactly like a Windows program." Asked, in full:
- 'Those' = the four window gaps: resize from every edge/corner (touch too), snapping (no overlap), keep windows on screen, drop a window on another to split.

The settings interface changes live with every selection.

builds.title: Run unless blocked: 2-min countdown → urgent alarm (red banner + loud AmberX ring) → 1-min grace → runs; Block anytime; zero session tokens
builds.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): 'Can you send notification that a command is about to be ran and I can intercept it from the banner and block it before axhub tries sending it.' HELD: queued, not started. Picks (cards): profile Refactor, held; countdown 2 minutes.

Design: a third tool policy next to allow / confirm, e.g. 'veto' (run unless blocked). A session's call returns a job id at once; axHub holds the call for the countdown (default 2 min, per-tool override possible later) and immediately pushes through the AmberX app (rule: all axHub pushes come from AmberX) and shows it in the console's banner (approvals banner or its own) with the reason title, the exact call, a live countdown, Block and Run now. No action = runs at zero. Block = cancelled, never runs, the session sees 'blocked' when it next looks at the job. Sessions never poll during the countdown: they carry on and read the job result once at the end only if they need it, which saves the re-read cost of approval checks. Approvals (confirm) stay for risky calls: deletes and free-form root shell. Brett picks which tools move to veto (proposal: merge-pr, redeploys, container restarts). Every veto call is logged with its outcome (ran / blocked / ran early) in the approvals history (approval-costs build). Related: approval-costs (history, wait call, resume), axhub-github-write.

origin.brief:
# Chat Viewer: every session stored, synced, searchable, exportable as 2-voice audio (Brett, Nov 1 ~3 AM)

Read CLAUDE.md, _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md, _claude/persona.md. Opus, one session. Git login works: plain `git push`. Merge origin/main first (other builds are landing).

Brett: store ALL our sessions (claude.ai text + voice chats, Claude Code sessions, headless build sessions) as transcripts in a viewer. When it loads, it checks for updates: new sessions, continued ones, changed ones, and updates the stored copies. Export any session as AUDIO with two separate voices: one for Brett, one for Claude (Amber).

IMPORTANT reality: claude.ai has no API to pull a user's chats, and we must NOT scrape claude.ai with Brett's login/cookies. Supported inputs:
1. Claude data export: Brett downloads it from claude.ai (Settings > Privacy > Export data) and uploads the zip (or conversations.json) in the viewer (phone file picker). Parse it, upsert by conversation uuid, detect new/changed by updated_at + message count/hash, keep versions.
2. Claude Code sessions: auto-sync the JSONL session files from ~/.claude/projects (root and axfbuild) on the VPS on a timer + on viewer load; incremental (byte offset/mtime).
3. Headless build logs (/root/axf-builds/*/*.log, /home/axfbuild/wt-*/*.log) as 'build sessions'.
4. Hub drop folder: Claude chat sessions can push conversations through axHub memory_write into project amberx-axf, area data, path `sessions/claude-ai/<uuid>.json` (schema below); the viewer ingests that folder too. Document the schema and add a line to _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md: when Brett says 'sync my chats', Claude uses recent_chats/read_conversation and writes each new/updated conversation there.

## Store
session@1 schema (framework/schemas + validators): id, source (claude-ai-text|claude-ai-voice|claude-code|headless|hub-drop), title, startedAt, updatedAt, project, messages [{role: user|assistant|tool, text, at, kind (speech|text|tool), toolName?}], hash, version history. Stored on the console data volume (SQLite or JSON files; your call, justify), not in git. Redact secrets (tokens/keys/passwords patterns) on ingest.
