origin.brief:
# GitHub App for the whole stack: one-click setup, tokens that never die (Brett, Nov 1 ~4 AM)

Read CLAUDE.md, _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md, _claude/persona.md. Opus, one session. Git login works: plain `git push`. Never print secrets (private keys, client secrets, tokens) anywhere: logs, reports, commits, screenshots.

Why: personal tokens keep dying (401s, 403s on the banner), and the current fine-grained token can't create repos (the axp-backup build at /root/axf-builds/axp-backup is waiting on 3 private repos: axp-xchat, axp-devstudio, axp-demo). Brett wants this fixed for good.

## 1. One-click setup (GitHub App Manifest flow)
- Console page (behind the existing auth wall, admin only): Settings > GitHub > 'Create GitHub App'. It POSTs a manifest to https://github.com/settings/apps/new (personal account MossesX): name 'AmberX AXF Bot' (add suffix if taken), homepage the console URL, redirect/callback to the console, no webhook needed (or webhook off), public: false.
- Permissions (repository): Administration RW, Contents RW, Pull requests RW, Actions RW, Workflows RW, Issues RW, Checks R, Commit statuses R, Metadata R.
- Callback: exchange the code (POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions), store app id, slug, client id, client secret, private key PEM and webhook secret in /opt/axf/.axf-console/github-app/ (dir 700, files 600, root-owned), never in git. Then send Brett to the install page (https://github.com/apps/<slug>/installations/new) with 'All repositories'. Detect the installation id after install (GET /app/installations with an app JWT).
- Also offer 'Authorize as Brett' (OAuth user-to-server via the same app, with refresh tokens, stored the same way): needed because INSTALLATION tokens cannot create repos on a personal account; user access tokens from the app with Administration write can (POST /user/repos). Refresh automatically (8 h access / 6 month refresh); banner when refresh fails.

## 2. Token broker
- framework/cli/github-token.mjs (+ a tiny Python twin for the console server if it needs it): `installation` -> mints a JWT from the PEM, exchanges for an installation token, caches it (refresh at 50 min), prints it only to stdout for callers; `user` -> the refreshed user access token.
- /usr/local/bin/axf-git-cred: use the installation token first, then the old GITHUB_TOKEN as fallback. `gh`: wrapper or GH_TOKEN via a helper so gh uses the app too. Keep the old token working as fallback until Brett deletes it.
- Point every GitHub caller at the broker: push banner, live-key-checks, activity banner GitHub part (the 403s), build_land/build_start paths, the console updater, CI-status reads. Repo creation (`axf repo create <name> --private`) uses the user token.
- axHub's github connector (MossesX/axHub, packages/connectors or the rest service config): add app-based auth via the same broker or its own JWT exchange; clone axHub next to the worktree, test (pnpm test, Node 22 via docker node:22), push its main, redeploy through Coolify the same way earlier builds did (token saved in the console, never printed). If that's too big, leave axHub on the old token and banner it as a follow-up.

## 3. Health + banner
- health@1 check: app key valid, installation present, installation token mints, user token refreshes, rate limit remaining. Red banner with the exact fix if any fail. Old-token expiry warning.
- After setup works: re-run the axp-backup push automatically (create the 3 private repos with the user token, then `bash /root/axp-backup/bin/backup.sh` or whatever finish script that build left; read /root/axf-builds/axp-backup/axp-backup.log and /root/axp-backup/REPORT.md first). Never commit secrets; the backup's own secret scan must pass.

Framework controls + theme/scale tokens only. Tests: manifest generation, callback exchange (mocked GitHub), file perms, JWT + token cache, git credential helper order + fallback, user-token refresh, health check states. Local test block from .github/workflows/android.yml + theme/controls/lifecycle checks. Phone + desktop screenshots of the setup page (no secrets on screen) to UI Review via framework/cli/shot.mjs, group 'GitHub App - Nov 1'. install_steps: new part 'GitHub App (no more tokens)' with the 3 taps. Commit, fetch+merge origin/main, retest, `git push origin HEAD:main` (never force). Report at _claude/builds/reports/github-app.md: what Brett taps, where things are stored (paths only), what now uses the app.

builds.title: Every UI element is a named asset
builds.detail:
Apply the rule across schemas/asset-types.json, the web and Android ports, the 39 starter assets and the conformance fixtures.

- Two tiers: element assets (button, slider, toggle, input, icon, label...) and parent assets (toolbar, menu, nav, app menu, dialog, container, window). A standalone element in a layout is its own named asset; groups only exist inside a parent asset.
- Namespaced ids for every asset (e.g. axf.button.save, axf.toolbar.editor); layouts and parents reference ids.
- Split instance (label, icon, action, state) from skin (style asset + theme tokens).
- Slots with type contracts in layout regions and parents; hot-swap and drag-and-drop = rebinding a slot to a compatible asset id.
- Kernel unchanged (open type registry).

notes.text: Overlaps settings-asset (new `settings` asset type, branch claude/project-thread-55oakl); build with settings-asset-fable.
Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Design note first: write `_claude/memory/docs/named-assets.md` — the two tiers (element assets: button, slider, toggle, input, icon, label; parent assets: toolbar, menu, nav, app-menu, dialog, container, window), the id namespace rule (`<ns>.<type>.<name>`, e.g. `axf.button.save`), instance vs skin split, and which existing starter ids change. List every file the rule touches. No code.

BRETT: review the design note. Decide (a) whether existing starter ids are renamed in place or aliased (old id keeps resolving), (b) whether element assets are required for every control or opt-in per app. Record both answers in the note and in `_claude/memory/decisions.md`.

Schema: in `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` add `"tier": "element" | "parent"` to every type and a top-level `idRule` (regex, documented) for namespaced ids; keep `optional: true` on new fields so old apps validate. Run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs schemas` and `axf validate --framework` — both must pass unchanged.

Validator (web): `framework/core/validate.ts` → `validateAsset` warns (not errors, until the switch flips) when an id does not match `idRule`; add `assetTier(type)`. Add 4 cases to `framework/spec/fixtures/validation.json` (good namespaced id, bare id, element, parent). `npx -y tsx framework/spec/gen-fixtures.mts` then CI check.

Validator (Kotlin + CLI): mirror the id rule in `framework/android/axf-kernel/.../asset/` validator and in the build-engine validator (`framework/cli/build-engine.mjs` validateAsset). Same fixture cases replayed by `ConformanceTest` (written without a compiler: check the "CI build errors" issue after push).

Element asset types, part 1: add `toggle`, `input`, `icon` as `tier: element` types in `asset-types.json` (data shape: label, icon, action, state keys; skin = style-theme tokens only). One starter each under `framework/assets/<type>/`. `axf validate --framework` passes.

Element asset types, part 2: mark the existing `button`, `slider`, `label` as `tier: element`; add the instance/skin split to their spec (`data.instance` {label, icon, action, state} vs `data.skin` {style tokens}) with the old flat shape still accepted by `asEnvelope` normalisation. Fixture cases in `components.json`.

Parent slots: in `asset-types.json` give every parent type (toolbar, app-menu, nav-menu, context-menu, dialog, container, window) a `slots` block like `layout.slots` (named slots + accepted element types), reusing `compileSlots`/`regionAccepts` from `framework/core/engines/layout.ts`. Fixture cases in `layout-slots.json` for one parent.

Rebinding = hot-swap: `framework/core/runtime.ts` gets `bindSlot(parentType, parentId, slot, elementId)` / `unbindSlot` (stored like `attachToHost` in `widgets.ts`, settings key `axf.bind.<parent>.<slot>`); `swap()` of a parent keeps bindings whose types still fit. Unit cases in `widgets.json` → `bindings`.

Kotlin runtime parity: `AxfRuntime.bindSlot/unbindSlot` + KV `<key>:bind` in the kernel, same rules as the TS version, replaying the `bindings` fixture in `ConformanceTest`. Written without a compiler; push and read the CI issue.

Rename the 39 starter assets to namespaced ids (`axf.<type>.<name>`) with the alias map chosen in step 2 (`framework/assets/aliases.json`, read by `registry.ts` + Kotlin `AssetRegistry`): every app manifest and `framework/defaults.json` still resolve. `axf validate --framework` + `validate apps/demo` + console `npm run build` pass.

React layer: `framework/react/components/Controls.tsx` renders an element asset by id (`<AssetButton id>` etc.) reading instance + skin; a standalone element in a layout region renders through the same path. Element Explorer (`react/studio/Inspector.tsx`) shows tier + bindings.

Compose layer: `axf-ui/components/Buttons.kt`, `Slider.kt`, `Controls.kt` take an element asset id the same way; `ElementExplorer.kt` shows tier + bindings. Android console showcase renders one bound element in its toolbar.

Flip the switch: `idRule` violations become errors for apps with `frameworkVersion` ≥ the new one (old apps keep warnings), `axf init` writes namespaced ids, templates updated. Run the CI template sweep locally (`axf init` for react-ts, next-ts, android-compose + validate).

Docs + close: `framework/spec/PORTING.md` section "Named assets"; CLAUDE.md Status bullet; decisions.md entry; mark the pending item complete and the plan feature built; differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/named-asset-rule.md` (rule for rebuilds).

builds.title: Port engine: bring a non-AXF app onto AmberX AXF (bake or rebuild)
builds.detail:
Runs the ports that claude-project parks (pending items port-<name>, manifest x.port, plan in the project at _claude/memory/docs/port-to-axf.md). Brett chose: ask each time between the two ways.

- bake: keep the codebase, run axf init into it (react-ts / next-ts / android-compose), then move its look and chrome into asset@1 assets step by step (colour/style themes, menus, toolbars, nav, dialogs, layout with region slots); UI reads engine tokens only (THEMING.md). Old styles go as each piece moves.
- rebuild: new AXF app from the closest boilerplate (axf boilerplates), old code kept alongside as reference, rebuilt feature by feature on assets/libraries/plugins.

Deliver: axf port <dir> --mode bake|rebuild (analysis report: what maps to which asset types, libraries, plugins; then staged codemods like ui-port.mjs does for UI kits), console + MCP drivers, manifest relation none -> built-on when it starts, fixtures/tests. steps.text: Spec first: `_claude/memory/docs/port-engine.md` — the two modes (bake / rebuild), the analysis report shape (`port-report@1`: stack, UI kit found, screens, chrome pieces → asset types, styles → tokens, libraries/plugins suggested, risk list), the staged codemod plan, and what `axf port` refuses (no manifest, dirty git tree). Read `framework/cli/ui-port.mjs` and `claude-project.mjs` first.

CLI entry: `framework/cli/port.mjs` + `axf port <dir> --mode bake|rebuild [--report-only] [--stage N]` in `axf.mjs`; `requireProject` gate; refuses without `--yes` when git is dirty; writes `port-report.json` next to the manifest. `--report-only` works on an empty folder (empty report).

Stack detection: reuse `claude-project.mjs` detection (react/next/android/python…), add UI-kit detection (MUI, Chakra, shadcn, Material3, Compose, Tailwind) by package.json / gradle deps; unit test with fixture folders under `framework/spec/fixtures/port/`.

Analysis, screens + chrome: scan routes/screens (React Router / Next pages / Compose NavHost) and chrome components (app bar, drawer, bottom nav, menus, toolbars, dialogs) → candidate asset list with target type and confidence. Report section `pieces`.

Analysis, styles → tokens: run `portSource` from `ui-port.mjs` in dry mode over the codebase to count colour/size literals and role usages; map to the token list from the theme engine; report `tokens` with unmapped literals. Cap files scanned (size + count) and skip node_modules/build.

Bake, stage 1: `axf init` into the existing project (template by stack) without overwriting app files (`src/axf/` + assets + manifest relation `built-on`), `axf.lock.json`; app still builds (the template guard allows an existing codebase). Checked with a fixture react app.

Bake, stage 2: themes — generate `color-theme` + `style-theme` assets from the detected palette (nearest tokens), apply the literal → `var(--fx-*)` codemod (`ui-port.mjs portSource`) to CSS/TSX/Kotlin files in place with a `.port-backup/`; `--stage 2` only; report lists every file changed.

Bake, stage 3: chrome — generate nav-menu / app-menu / toolbar / dialog assets from the detected pieces and swap the components for the framework ones (`AppShell` / Compose `AppShell`), old components kept under `legacy/` until removed; `--stage 3`.

Rebuild mode: pick the closest boilerplate (`framework/boilerplates/index.json` tags vs detected features), `axf init --boilerplate` into `<dir>-axf` beside the old code, write `PORT-PLAN.md` with screen-by-screen mapping and the old file for each; report `rebuild.plan`.

Drivers: engine-rpc `port` / `port-report`, console `POST /api/port` + `GET /api/port/report?dir=`, MCP `app_port(dir, mode, stage)` (write, needs the console token); manifest `framework.relation` none → built-on when stage 1 runs (`project.mjs` validates).

Console view: Plugins → **Port** (or Wizards view section): pick a folder from allowed roots (project-wizard's `AXF_WIZARD_ROOTS` rule), run the report, show pieces/tokens tables, run stages one at a time with the file list and a diff count; rebuild plan rendered as a checklist.

Pending items hook: `port-<name>` items (parked by claude-project) get a "Run port" button in Pending rows (slot `pending.item`) that opens the console view on that project; `claude-project` writes `x.port.engine: "axf port"` into the manifest.
First real target, xGallery (MossesX/xGallery, React 19 + Express + SQLite): BRETT attaches the repo; run `--report-only`, review the report together, record the mode choice. No codemod yet.
xGallery bake stage 1–2 on a branch in that repo (init + themes), app builds; note unmapped literals; push branch `axf-port` for Brett to look at on the phone.
Tests: `framework/spec/check-port.mjs` over the fixture folders (detection, report shape, stage 1 idempotent, stage 2 backup + dry run, refusals: no manifest, dirty tree, symlinks); CI line.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/app-port-engine.md`, LOG.md, CLAUDE.md Status + `axf port` in Build/run/test, pending complete; decisions.md note on bake vs rebuild defaults.

builds.title: Plugin conflict alarm + tracked AI patches + installed add-ons list
builds.detail:
Brett, Oct 18 2026 (parked as unsafe: AI patching and cascading uninstalls need design and review before anyone builds it):

1. When a plugin could potentially conflict with another plugin, raise a developer alarm (alerts library, source conflicts) shown as an expandable row grid like the Systems check grid: same kinds of details per row, fix instructions and external links.
2. Each conflict row has 3 badges/actions: (a) uninstall a plugin - choose which one; (b) ignore; (c) use AI to patch the conflict. The patch must NOT alter any plugin source.
3. Patches are tracked and listed in an Installed add-ons list that covers plugins, add-ons, modules, libraries and patches. Installing a patch is tracked and the patch can be removed.
4. Removing a patch uninstalls every conflicting plugin it patched; those plugins must then be reinstalled.

Builds on: alerts library (conflicts source, diagnostics: same asset id / setting key / settings tab from two named modules; plugins:dup ids on the server), plugin-lifecycle@1 (install/uninstall scripts, backups), plugin-manager (Fable, pending), agent manager add-ons (agent-addon@1 install/uninstall tracking), axf.llm@1 for the AI patch.
Open questions for Brett at build time: what counts as a potential conflict beyond the runtime diagnostics (routes, capability services, settings keys, assets, nav ids, CSS prefixes, data dirs?); where patches live (an overlay layer the console applies at load, never the plugin folder); whether removing a patch should back up the plugins first and offer one-tap reinstall.

origin.said: AI patching and cascading uninstalls need design and review before anyone builds it):

steps.text: Design note, part 1 (no code): `_claude/memory/docs/plugin-conflicts.md` — what counts as a potential conflict beyond runtime diagnostics: routes (`/api/plugins/<f>/`), capability services (two providers of one `axf.x@1`), settings keys, asset ids, nav ids, CSS prefixes (`axp-*`), data dirs, Python module names. For each: how it is detected from `plugin.json` + the bundle + `plugin-inventory@1` facts, severity, false-positive risk.

Design note, part 2: patches. Proposal: a patch is an **overlay** (`.axf-console/patches/<id>/patch.json`, `plugin-patch@1`: target plugins, kind rename-route / remap-setting / alias-asset / disable-contribution, applied by the console at load, never touching a plugin folder); AI only proposes a patch document, a person approves it (change-batch card); removal backs up + offers one-tap reinstall. Risks and what is refused.

BRETT reviews both notes and answers the three open questions (conflict kinds in scope, overlay approach yes/no, backup + reinstall on patch removal). Status stays `unsafe` until he says the design is approved; then `pending`. Record in decisions.md.

Conflict engine (pure): extend `framework/core/engines/plugins.ts` (`plugin-inventory@1`) with `potentialConflicts(records)` for the approved kinds, severity + fix hints; Kotlin `PluginInventoryEngine` + Python `plugin-manager/server/engine.py` mirror it; fixture cases in `spec/fixtures/plugin-inventory.json` → `conflicts` (`check-plugin-inventory.mts`, `test.py`, `PluginInventoryConformanceTest`).

Alerts source `conflicts`: `apps/console-web/server/alerts.py` raises one alert per conflict key (`conflict:<kind>:<a>:<b>`, warn, resolved when it disappears) from the engine output every poll; rule default: bell on. Test in `server/test_alerts.py`.

Conflict grid UI: plugin `apps/console-web/plugins/plugin-conflicts` (from `_template`) with a dialog `plugin-conflicts.grid` built on the Systems check grid component pattern (expandable rows: details, fix instructions, links); opened from the alert's link and from Plugin Manager rows. Read-only this step.

Row actions (a) Uninstall — pick which plugin, confirm by typing its folder, runs `plugin-lifecycle.mjs uninstall --all` through the existing `/api/plugin-lifecycle/<folder>/uninstall`; (b) Ignore — stored per conflict key in the plugin dataDir, hides the row and resolves the alert; both admin-only.

Patch overlay runtime: `server/patches.py` loads `plugin-patch@1` files, validates them against the schema (`framework/schemas/plugin-patch.json`), applies approved kinds at plugin load (route prefix rename, settings key remap, asset alias, contribution disable) in the loader, never writes into plugin folders; `GET /api/plugins/plugin-conflicts/patches`.

(c) AI patch: "Patch with AI" asks Mosses through `axf.llm@1` for a patch document for this conflict (prompt includes the engine facts), validates it, shows it on a change-batch-style approval card; Apply writes the file and reloads plugins; refused when the assistant is off (409 with what is missing).

Installed add-ons list: dialog + Settings → Plugins → Add-ons listing plugins, libraries (`plugin-inventory`), modules, agent add-ons (`agent-addon@1` from `axf.agents@1` when present) and patches, each with installed date, what it touches, Remove. Patches show which plugins they patch.

Patch removal: Remove patch → backup (`.axf-console/plugin-backups/`) → uninstall every plugin it patched (lifecycle) → list them with one-tap Reinstall from the catalog (`plugin-catalog.mjs install`) when the step-3 decision says so. Audit line per action.
Tests: plugin `test.py` (grid data, ignore, patch validation + refusals, removal cascade with fake lifecycle), engine fixtures, lifecycle check, CI lines.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/plugin-conflicts.md`, LOG.md, web screenshots, CLAUDE.md Status, rules line about patches never touching plugin folders, pending complete.

- Needs the axHub repo (MossesX/axHub) attached.

origin.brief:
# Dev Console as an Android app: wrapper, one codebase (Brett, Nov 7)

Brett chose the wrapper over a native rewrite: the existing web console runs inside an Android app shell, same way AmberX loads its web plugins. One codebase; every console change shows on the phone at once.

Reuse: orchestrator build `console-android-app-tabs` (19 steps, pending) — get its brief (`node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs brief console-android-app-tabs`) and use what fits; ignore the archived native rewrite `console-android-native-tabs`. Reuse AmberX's Android shell/bridge pieces (apps/amberx-droid) rather than writing new ones.

1. Android app shell loading the console (console.amberxai.com), with sign-in kept, back button/navigation, pull-to-refresh, offline screen.
2. Native bridges where needed: push notifications (build start/finish/fail/land alerts), mic for voice, background wake, file share/download (APKs), deep links that open a console screen.
3. Console UI stays asset-driven; phone layouts come from the existing three-layouts/phone assets, no hard-coded styling.
4. APK built in CI next to amberx-debug.apk; listed under Apps in the console/axHub for install.
5. UI Review with three options (--choices) for the shell chrome. Tests. Add to Shipped features.

Progress: append `<time> START|DONE <step>` to PROGRESS.md here at each step; don't stop between steps. Commit, don't push.

3c. Patches views: three routes (console / pilot / axhub) each rendering the holder's WebView for that tab; the Patches banner (logo, day/night switch, clock, settings button) is the one banner; hub sign-in via the developer-app waiting screen (shared cookie store = one session for every tab); Settings → Patches group: hub address, each tab's URL, reload tab, open in the phone's browser.

Problem: the same data lives in 3+ places (builds store, per-profile orchestrator files, pending list, journal, plans, tracker/catalog, feature-ledger, origins) read by different tools, constantly out of sync.

origin.said:
# Style override rule (Brett, Nov 7) — contract + enforcement

The rule:
1. Main apps — Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX, Patches — SHARE one style/theme/design. Their override switch is OFF by default.
2. Every plugin and every UI asset has its own override switch, ON by default. On first install it stores its own copy seeded from the shared style, so everything looks the same until someone changes it.
3. A plugin/asset override changes ONLY that plugin/asset. It never changes the app it belongs to, other plugins, or the shared style.
4. Turning a plugin's override OFF makes it follow its app's (shared) style live.
5. Turning an app's override ON gives that app its own style; its plugins keep their own copies.

Do:
- Find the existing pieces (app-style-override branch/build, apply-all-levels, appearance-asset-tokens, skins, theme engine, settings assets) and reuse them; finish app-style-override if it fits.
- Implement the resolution order in the shared theme/style engine (both web and Android twins where they exist): asset own copy (if override on) → app (if app override on) → shared main style.
- Switch in each app's and each plugin's settings (settings asset, no hard-coded UI). Migration: existing plugins get override ON with a copy of the current shared style; apps OFF.
- Write the rule to RULES.md and the brief template so every build follows it. CI check: every UI asset/plugin declares the override field.
- UI Review: submit the switch UI with three options (--choices).
- Tests for each rule above. Add to Shipped features.

builds.title: URGENT: rebuild pipeline — orchestrator IDs, splits, Pending→Queue, slot-driven headless launches
builds.detail:
Rebuild the build pipeline from scratch:
1. Everything Brett asks for becomes a build sent to the orchestrator.
2. Orchestrator assigns a build ID.
3. Orchestrator uses Claude to split it into steps (<=30 min) and picks a model per step: Fable only when needed, Opus otherwise.
4. Build goes to Pending. Brett moves Pending -> Queue.
5. Orchestrator watches the VPS: connected Claude accounts, which have Fable, max parallel and free slots per account.
6. Whenever a slot opens, the orchestrator grabs the next build in the Queue and starts a headless session on it: Fable steps to an account with Fable, everything else to Opus accounts. Never launches right away, only when a slot is free.
7. Steps tick off in the progress files per existing rules; a monitor watches them and updates progress live.

And uh, if it's a account that has Fable, he'll send the Fable to that. He'll send everything else to Opus. He will, no, he will check the BPS to see what accounts have what slots. Available parallel. Dish out the steps, okay? The steps are marked. We already have the rules for how the steps are marked down into a, in a progress pile and blah blah blah. ## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-08T16:57:58.978Z
> Brett wants everything in ONE app. Molly becomes the single shell for every app and plugin: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX, and all future apps. Patches is scrapped. NO embedding: Do NOT embed other apps as pages/iframes (no second file menu/banner/chrome). ONE native app: Molly has the only chrome (one banner, one file menu, one nav, one settings). Every app's screens, plugins, menus and settings load natively into Molly as plugins, merged into Molly's single menu/nav. Menus: Molly's menus reach EVERYTHING from every app: every screen, plugin, action, setting. Grouped by app and category, search/jump-to-anything, favorites and recents, sliding sub menus, three-dot overflow on small screens. Fully voice and API controllable. Layouts: User picks a layout mode. IDE-style is ONE option among others. In the IDE layout, containers dock/split/float/resize, and each container can optionally be a tab group: drag anything from a menu onto a container and it opens there as a new tab; tabs drag between containers. Save/switch named layouts. Reuse framework tab group / drag-to-tab work.

## What to build
Continue build "Molly is the one native shell for every app (no embedding); all-apps menus; layout modes with IDE + tab-group containers; Patches leftovers retired" (molly-one-shell) [Molly] — Phase 3, model Opus.

Brett said (2026-11-08 16:57):
"Brett wants everything in ONE app. Molly becomes the single shell for every app and plugin: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX, and all future apps. Patches is scrapped. NO embedding: Do NOT embed other apps as pages/iframes (no second file menu/banner/chrome). ONE native app: Molly has the only chrome (one banner, one file menu, one nav, one settings). Every app's screens, plugins, menus and settings load natively into Molly as plugins, merged into Molly's single menu/nav. Menus: Molly's menus reach EVERYTHING from every app: every screen, plugin, action, setting. Grouped by app and category, search/jump-to-anything, favorites and recents, sliding sub menus, three-dot overflow on small screens. Fully voice and API controllable. Layouts: User picks a layout mode. IDE-style is ONE option among others. In the IDE layout, containers dock/split/float/resize, and each container can optionally be a tab group: drag anything from a menu onto a container and it opens there as a new tab; tabs drag between containers. Save/switch named layouts. Reuse framework tab group / drag-to-tab work."
This phase downgrades Fable → Opus: fine, no approval needed (it is recorded when you tick its first step).

Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.

origin.said: Brief (headless launch, no verbatim block): Account failover + phone alerts + one home per login. 1. Automatic failover: when a build fails on an account for auth (expired/unrefreshable login) or usage limit, immediately mark that account out and relaunch the same build on the next available account (workers, then the interactive account; API accounts only per routing rules). No build should die and stay dead because of one account. Today three builds died in 1 s each on account-1 (OAuth expired) and nothing retried. 2. Phone notification (AmberX) on every such problem: which account, what failed (expired login / limit / no credits), which build moved where, and what Brett needs to do (e.g. sign account-1 in). 3. One home per login: each account's credentials live in exactly ONE store; every token refresh from any build, console or session writes back to that same place. No duplicate copies that can spend a refresh token and leave others dead. Audit claude-login.mjs / claude-token-save.mjs / claude-headless.sh and the console AI keys store for duplicates; find why account-1's refresh failed (spent by another copy vs idle expiry) and report it. 4. Status in the console Claude accounts screen: out/why/until, last refresh time per login.

steps.text: Failover engine: classify auth / limit / no-credits from the run log, mark the account out (why, until), pick the next account (workers, then interactive, API per routing); launcher relaunches on any account, not only workers; tests
Phone alert on every account problem through axf.notify@1 / the alert hub (AmberX push): account, what failed, where the build went, what Brett must do; notify.json entry; tests

One home per login: audit claude-login / token-save / headless / AI keys copies, make ~/.claude-accounts/<name> the single home every refresh writes to, record last refresh per login; find why account-1's refresh failed; tests
Console: Claude accounts status (out / why / until, last refresh), routes + MCP/voice commands, settings section (failover + alerts); tests
UI Review (3 options as assets), report, STATUS, THREADS, PR

builds.title: Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job
builds.detail: When the orchestrator receives a job and splits it into steps, it first checks the Shipped features ledger (which must hold every feature the orchestrator has ever built). It must: not build anything twice; not break or redo anything already done; and if a step would conflict with or change something already built, notify Brett (AmberX notification) and wait before going on. Make the Shipped features ledger complete (backfill every landed build) and keep it updated on every land. Also standing rule: ONLY the orchestrator launches builds, picks model and account, owns pending/queue and monitors status; voice/chat sessions only hand it requests.

notes.text: Conflict flow (Brett): a conflicting step is moved to a special Conflicts section and removed from the build; the other steps still build. Brett gets an AmberX notification-panel item that explains the conflict and offers suggested resolutions; he taps a suggestion or types a prompt, which goes to the orchestrator, and the orchestrator makes a new build from it. Then test it: Brett will send a 3-4 step build that deliberately overlaps existing shipped features to confirm the orchestrator catches it.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett (Nov 9): "needs a way to go through all the pending builds and the build queue and search for steps that are gonna break existing work or conflict with it, or it's already done, or it doesn't need it anymore." Add a Sweep: a button on the builds page (and API/voice: 'sweep the builds') plus an automatic run on every land. It checks every step of every pending and queued build against the Shipped features ledger, main's code, and the other pending/queued builds, and flags each step: Already done (shipped by build X), Conflicts (would change/break feature Y, shows the files and lines), Duplicate (same as a step in build Z), Obsolete (no longer needed: superseded or its target was removed), OK. Results: badges on each build and step, a Sweep report with a filter per flag, and one-tap fixes per flag: drop step, merge into the other build, move to Conflicts for Brett, keep. Nothing is changed without Brett's tap. Cheap first pass in plain code (ledger + file overlap); Claude only for the unclear ones.

Correction (Brett): the Sweep does NOT run automatically on every land. It runs only (1) when Brett runs it (button / API / voice), and (2) by the orchestrator on a single build at two points: when it receives the job, and again right before it dispatches it (launches the session). Flags found at dispatch hold the build for Brett instead of launching.

Merged with orchestrator-checks-each-build-against-main-righ for the 'never build twice' part: every build is now checked against main (Shipped features, its PR, its branch, the files its steps create) right before it is queued and again at dispatch; done = closed, partly done = only what is left is queued. Still open here: the check at split time, the AmberX conflict notice and the ledger backfill.

Continue build "Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job" (orchestrator-checks-shipped-features-before-spli) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"when he get receives a job, he splits it up into steps. And when he does that, he needs to make sure he needs to check with the shipped features... he needs to make sure he's not doing something twice or fucking up something that's already been done and if it's gonna conflict with something or change something that's already built he's gonna let me know"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.

origin.said: Account health probe + failover + phone alerts (Brett). A. Health probe (new): On console load and on a schedule, the orchestrator probes EVERY Claude account (subscriptions + API keys): a tiny headless session with a minimal brief, NO rules, NO CLAUDE.md, no MCP. It checks: login valid, credits/usage available (5-hour + weekly used/left, reset times; API: balance or last-known spend vs cap), which models it can use (opus/fable/etc.). It saves each account's status in ONE shared store all plugins read (status: ok / limited / no credits / login expired; credits left; models; checked at). Usage badge, Claude accounts screen and routing all read it. Keep probe cost near zero. The orchestrator only sends a job to an account that the store says can take it, with the model it needs. B. Failover: If a build still fails on auth or limit, mark the account out, update the store, and relaunch the same build on the next able account. Today 5 builds died in 1-3 s on account-1 (expired) and account-3 Hulu (no credits) and nothing retried. C. Phone alerts (AmberX): Notify on every account problem: which account, what (expired / limit / no credits), which build moved where, what Brett must do. D. One home per login: Each account's credentials live in exactly ONE store; every token refresh from any build/console/session writes back there. Audit claude-login.mjs, claude-token-save.mjs, claude-headless.sh, console AI keys for duplicate copies; find why account-1's refresh failed and report. Rules: Full API + voice + MCP/CLI control; settings in categorized collapsible sections (probe interval, alerts); tests; report, STATUS, THREADS. E. Probe notifications (Brett): When the console loads: send a phone notification that the account checks are about to run; when done, send another with the result per account (ok / limited / no credits / expired, credits left, models). Uses the AmberX notification panel (build amberx-notify-panel) as its type 'account-status'.

origin.brief:
# Build: orchestrator-api-rule-in-every-brief-plan-studio

## Brett said (verbatim)
> Now I want to make sure he makes the orchestrator is going to include in the briefs, everything comes with an API. It also needs to make the stepped plan in Plan Studio for the build. And it needs to update any plan in the Plan Studio. So the Plan Studio needs to be uh, somehow synced with future builds.

## What to build
Continue build "Orchestrator: API rule in every brief + Plan Studio stepped plans, always in sync" (orchestrator-api-rule-in-every-brief-plan-studio) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"Now I want to make sure he makes the orchestrator is going to include in the briefs, everything comes with an API. It also needs to make the stepped plan in Plan Studio for the build. And it needs to update any plan in the Plan Studio. So the Plan Studio needs to be uh, somehow synced with future builds."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.

builds.title: Headless loop guards: stop endless loops and searches
builds.detail: Guards on every headless session the orchestrator launches (claude-headless.sh + agent-slots + the running-builds watchdog's afterTick hook in pipeline.mjs): 1) Hard caps per session: --max-turns, wall time and cost cap derived from the step estimates (e.g. 2x estimate), settings with defaults. 2) Step progress timer: no step tick within 1.5x the step's estimate -> warn note, at 2x -> stop the session, build back to pending with the reason. 3) Loop detector reading the live log: the same command/tool call (or near-identical grep/find/sed) repeated N times, or M searches in a row with no edit/commit -> stop and note. 4) Search budget per step (e.g. 15 greps/finds) written into the brief and enforced by the detector. 5) Every stop: build note with the reason and last log lines, AmberX notification (normal notification, not an alarm), slot released, no auto-relaunch of a looped step until Brett says. 6) Brief line: 'If you can't find something in 3 searches, stop and leave a note.' Settings in orchestrator settings (categorized sections), full API/MCP/CLI/voice control. Tests with fake logs: repeated command, search spree, no tick, cost cap.

builds.title: Reserve build IDs at once: add returns the ID with the veto countdown
builds.detail: Today pending_change add (and control_add on planner.builds/plans) is held on the 90 s veto countdown and the orchestrator only assigns the build ID when it runs, so callers (Claude sessions) must guess the ID from the title to add notes. Fix: the orchestrator (ID registry) reserves the ID the moment the call arrives, before the hold, and returns it in the held result (e.g. reservedId). Notes, sub prompts and status calls on a reserved ID queue up and apply in order once the add runs; if Brett denies the add, the reservation and anything queued on it are dropped. IDs never collide (registry check). Same for plan_park and plan_add. Tests: add returns the id while held; a note on the reserved id lands after the add; deny drops both.

steps.text: Design the reservation model in the orchestrator's ID registry. Add a `reserved` state with reservedAt, origin call, kind (build|plan) and holdId. steps.text: Change the veto-hold contract so the ID is reserved before the hold starts. Held results carry reservedId, holdId and secondsLeft. Queue notes, sub prompts and status calls that target a reserved ID. The note, sub prompt and status handlers check whether the ID is reserved and, if so, add the op to the queue instead of failing. The queued result says queued:true with its seq. Replay applies the ops in order after the add runs.

Also a 'find the session where we talked about X' command that ranks sessions by match. Tapping a hit opens the recorder at that moment and plays the audio. Plain search also drops filler phrases like 'find the session where', 'when we talked about' so a whole sentence still works, zero tokens.

Brett: "With the keywords in focus." In the scrolling results window each snippet is centered on the matched keywords, highlighted. Opening a hit scrolls the transcript so the keyword is centered on screen, highlighted and focused, with next/previous match buttons inside that session.

Brett: "there's a column on the left with all the hits. All the sessions that match: the session name and the type of thing we were talking about." Results window layout: left column lists every session with hits (session name, date, hit count, and a topic tag for what it was about, e.g. builds, skins, approvals, AmberX); tapping one shows its hits on the right, keywords centered and highlighted. Topic tags: from the linked Claude session's title and the builds it touched (plain code, zero tokens); optionally a cheap one-time tag per session after transcription, off by default.

Brett: "I want a RAG database made of all the transcripts." Build a RAG store over every transcript: chunk each transcript (with session, date, timestamps, speaker, topic tags), embed the chunks with a local embedding model on the VPS (no Claude tokens), store them in Postgres with pgvector (reuse the postgres-console container plan if it exists, else its own table), and index every new transcript automatically after transcription. Two ways in: 1) semantic search (meaning, not just exact words) in the same results window, mixed with the keyword hits; 2) 'Ask' (API/MCP/voice): Claude or Gizmo retrieve the top chunks and answer with the sessions and timestamps as sources, each linking to that moment. Share the store with the Agent Manager's RAG knowledge (agent-profile build) so employees can use it. Settings: on/off, re-index, what gets indexed. notes.text: ROOT CAUSE (found live): deploy/claude-workers.mjs liveSessions() runs `tmux ls`; when NO tmux sessions exist, tmux exits non-zero ('no server running'), so it returns null = 'can't ask tmux'. Then ledger() counts every open session as running and liveClaims keeps claims for 12 h. So the stale entries survive exactly when nothing is running. Fix: treat 'no server running' (tmux present, exit 1) as an empty Set; only return null when tmux binary is missing. Test it.

Root cause fixed in PR #406 (claude/orch-self-check-stuck): tmux 'no server running' was read as unknown, so every unclosed session in events.jsonl counted as running. Self-check on console load and stuck ticks releases dead claims, expired limits and builds with no session; tests in claude-workers.test.mjs and pipeline.test.mjs; each release logged.

builds.title: Split builds pages (Build Manager = Pending + Complete; Orchestrator = Queued + Active) with one clean shared table design
builds.detail:
Replaces one-builds-page-pending-queued-built-tabs-remove (mark superseded).

Pages: Build Manager owns Pending (create, edit, prioritize, Send to orchestrator) and Complete (finished builds sent back by the orchestrator: account that actually built it, model, cost, PR, land status). Build orchestrator owns only Queued and Active (route, assign account, hold, cancel/return to Pending); finished builds go back to Build Manager Complete. Remove every other builds table and the separate Build queue screen (redirect).

Design: one shared framework build-table asset used by all four tabs so they look the same. Each build is one clean compact line (title, priority, status badge, steps done/total, account, model) that expands; inside the expanded row, collapsible sections/sub-grids (steps with state, runs/sessions, cost, files/PR, Brett's words, log tail). Per-tab columns differ only where needed: Active shows a live elapsed timer, steps complete with a progress bar, current step, account actually running it; Queued shows position and why it's waiting; Complete shows duration, cost, who built it. Clean, minimal, theme tokens only, phone and desktop. Screenshots to UI Review. Full API/voice control.

builds.title: Saved Claude logins never end up on a spent refresh token
builds.detail: Builds run on a per-build copy of a saved login (claude-login.mjs). Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). Fix: find every path where the rotation is lost (crash, kill, exit 1, sweep timing, two builds refreshing the same login at once), write rotations back atomically with a lock, never let two copies refresh the same login concurrently, and before launch check the saved login is alive; if dead, skip that account, alert the phone, and don't burn runs on it. Tests for each path.

Drag tabs between groups, and drag chunks onto each other or into a pack template to build new skins and assets. 5) SPLIT TAB: any tab can split into editor plus live preview, with real-time updates while editing. 6) Layouts can be saved and restored. And the ability to view them side by side, multiple containers with tab groups, mix and match elements in multiple floating containers to compare side by side. An IDE-style thing with a bunch of floating tab groups with different types of assets in them, with the info on the chunk, and you can drag them to each other and build new things side by side. Each tab can be split with a preview and an editor so you can see changes in real time.

steps.text: Design the chunk preview and demo contract and the studio layout schema. Chunk manifest fields: demo capability (interactive kind: behaviour, layout or component; sandbox entry; rendered-preview fallback) and a thumbnail spec. Studio layout document: tab groups (docked or floating, position and size), tabs (asset ref, type, split state), compare containers, and named saved layouts. Add a migration that upgrades the existing IDE layout settings from walkthrough-player-ide-layout and the skin section-package manifests from skins-as-section-packages.
steps.why: Schema and migration design shared by the skins, demo and studio ports

steps.text: Extend the framework IDE layout engine taken from walkthrough-player-ide-layout. Tab groups become dockable or floating. Groups hold tabs of any asset type through a tab-type registry. Tabs can be dragged between groups and between docked and floating groups. Groups can be nested into compare containers. All of this is driven by the new layout document.

steps.text: Add the split-tab primitive and the live-update channel. Any tab can split into an editor pane and a preview pane. steps.text: Add server-side preview rendering for skin chunks and UI assets: a cached thumbnail renderer and a full-preview render endpoint. Thumbnails are invalidated when a chunk changes. Reuse the UI asset designer renderer.

Add a preview action to every list and grid that shows skin chunks or assets: the skins section-package lists, pack grids, the UI asset designer library and the demonstration designer pickers. Hovering shows a thumbnail and Preview opens a full preview pane.

Add full API control for preview. Deep link console_open target skins/preview/<chunk>. Readable preview state. Actions preview.open, preview.close and preview.thumbnail. All of it reachable the same way through REST routes, MCP console actions and plugin commands, the CLI and AmberX voice intents.

Add the interactive demo. Demo opens a live sandbox for demoable chunks (behaviour, layouts, components) by reusing the Demonstration designer sandbox, so you can actually use the chunk. Chunks that cannot be demoed fall back to a rendered preview. The Demo action is added next to Preview in every list and grid.

Add full API control for demo. Deep link console_open skins/demo/<chunk>. Readable sandbox state (running, mode interactive or rendered). Actions demo.open, demo.reset and demo.close. All of it reachable through REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

Add the compare view. Open any number of chunks side by side in containers that can be docked or floating. Containers can mix asset types, and each container is a tab group from the extended layout engine.

Add the IDE studio as an optional view, off by default and switched on with a setting, not forced. Add drag-to-compose in the studio. Dropping a chunk onto another chunk, or into a pack template, creates a new skin or asset draft through the UI asset designer and the skins section-package builder, then opens the draft in a new tab.

Wire split tabs into the studio and compare views for every asset tab type. Each type gets an editor and a live preview that updates in real time over the live-preview channel, with a split toggle on every tab.

Add saving and restoring of layouts. Named studio and compare layouts can be saved, listed, restored, renamed and deleted. They are stored per profile and the last-used layout is restored automatically.

Add full API control for compare, the studio, split tabs, compose and layouts. Deep links: console_open skins/studio, skins/compare?chunks=… and skins/studio?layout=…. Readable state: groups, tabs, split state, info panel. Actions: open, close and move tabs; float and dock groups; split and unsplit; compose; layout save, restore and delete; the studio-view setting. builds.title: One VPS plugin: everything VPS in one place (gauges, banner widget with heat-colour icons and dropdown, cleanup, settings, status)
builds.detail: ONE VPS plugin (e.g. 'VPS'), reachable from Maintenance and its own nav entry. 1) CONSOLIDATE: find every VPS-related feature across the console and move it into this plugin as tabs or sections, leaving no duplicates behind. That includes the claude-badge VPS check, agent-slots resource and swap settings and warnings, the VPS settings/orchestrator-only rule plugin (from vps-orchestrator-only-rule-vps-settings-console), Docker/container views, container-access, the Coolify/Hostinger links, VPS terminal shortcuts, ai-keys VPS sync, maintenance cleanup/redundancy scans, the disk alerts, and the running-builds watchdog's resource bits. Old entry points redirect to the new plugin. 2) STATUS tab: live gauges and meters for CPU load (1/5/15 min), RAM, swap, disk per filesystem, plus Docker per-container CPU/RAM and the top processes. Several views (radial, bars, compact strip, history sparklines), switchable and remembered, with adjustable thresholds. 3) BANNER WIDGET: a snappable widget for the banner, toolbars and title bars, with modes icon only, icon plus value, or mini meters. It has its own settings (metrics, mode, thresholds, refresh). 4) ICON-ONLY HEAT COLOUR: each icon's colour follows its level on a smooth scale, white (low) to gray to black to red (high). The stops are editable and the theme can override them. 5) BANNER DROPDOWN: clicking any banner gauge opens a dropdown listing every gauge, one row each: a dot in the same heat colour as that gauge, the name (Load, RAM, Swap, Disk /), the percentage, and the actual values (e.g. 9.4 / 16 GB). Rows update live, the clicked one is highlighted, and the footer has Open VPS plugin and quick cleanup links. 6) CLEANUP tab: docker builder/image/container prune, apt/npm/pip caches, journal vacuum, old build worktrees and logs, /tmp, the Playwright cache, and stale git locks. Each has a size preview and a confirm, shows the space freed and logs to the fix log. Optional auto-cleanup over a threshold (off by default). 7) SETTINGS tab: every VPS setting in one place. Plain code, no AI. Full REST, MCP, CLI and voice control. Desktop and phone screenshots go to UI Review.

Show the active window and let it be cancelled early. Full API control.

origin.said: I need a settings on the approval page to allow all for the next hour or two hours or a custom field that I can enter, or deny all for a custom field. Until a certain time or amount of time. And where's the switch? A setting to control the time of the 90 seconds.

steps.text: Design the approval policy schema and migration: a 'window' record (mode allow|deny, starts_at, ends_at, created_by, source ui|rest|mcp|cli|voice, cancelled_at) and a 'veto_countdown_sec' setting (default 90, bounds 10–3600). Only one active window at a time; a new window replaces the old one. Write the migration so existing installs keep 90 s and have no window. Document the contract in the approvals schema doc.
steps.why: Schema + migration design for persisted approval policy shared by server, MCP, CLI and voice

steps.text: Engine: before an approval is queued, check the active window. In an allow window, auto-approve it; in a deny window, auto-deny it. Log every auto-decision with the window id. Expire windows lazily on read and with a timer so expiry clears without a restart. Replace the hard-coded 90 s veto countdown with the veto_countdown_sec setting, read when each countdown starts.

Policy service: setWindow({mode, duration|until}), cancelWindow(), getPolicy() returning the active window with remaining time, and get/set veto_countdown_sec. Validate inputs: until must be in the future, duration must be within 24 h unless forced, countdown must be within bounds. Emit change events so the UI and phone notifications update live.

REST routes: GET /api/approvals/policy, POST /api/approvals/policy/window ({mode:'allow'|'deny', minutes | until}), DELETE /api/approvals/policy/window, GET/PUT /api/approvals/policy/veto-countdown. Use the existing console auth and audit logging.

Approval page UI, settings section: 'Allow all for' with 1 h and 2 h presets, a custom duration field and an until-time picker; 'Deny all for' with a custom duration and an until-time picker; a 'Veto countdown' number field (seconds, defaults to 90) with a save button. Use the plugin framework components and call the REST routes from the previous step.

Approval page UI, active-window banner: show the mode (allow or deny), a live countdown to the end time and the end time itself, plus a 'Cancel now' button. Show the same badge in the axHub header while a window is active. Update live from the policy change events.

API part for the UI (deep links and state): register console_show / console_open targets approvals/settings, approvals/settings#window and approvals/settings#veto-countdown. Expose the policy state through console state read. Add MCP console actions approvals.policy.get, approvals.window.set, approvals.window.cancel, approvals.vetoCountdown.get and approvals.vetoCountdown.set, all backed by the same policy service.

CLI and voice: add `axf approvals allow --for 2h|--until 18:30`, `axf approvals deny --for 30m|--until …`, `axf approvals window cancel`, `axf approvals status` and `axf approvals veto-countdown [<sec>]`. Add AmberX voice intents with the same meanings, for example 'allow all approvals for two hours', 'deny all until 6 pm', 'cancel the approval window', 'set veto countdown to 60 seconds' and 'what's the approval window', each confirmed by voice. Both go through the REST API.

Tests: policy service (set, replace, expire and cancel a window; validation), engine auto-approve/deny inside a window and normal flow outside it, configurable countdown, REST routes, MCP actions, CLI parsing of durations and until times, and the voice intent parse. Add a UI test for the settings form and the banner cancel button.

Final: run the full test suite. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/approval-page-allow-all-deny-all-for-a-set-time.md, including an API table showing how each feature is reached through the deep link, state read, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. builds.detail: 1) Uninstall/remove the Build Manager plugin. Audit its responsibilities first and hand each to the orchestrator (or the right owner); nothing lost. Supersedes split-builds-pages-build-manager-pending-complet-2. 2) Orchestrator screen tabs: Pending (everything it's been asked to do), Queue, Active, Incomplete, Complete, Errors. 3) Splitting happens right away when a build is filed, so the Queue shows steps. builds.detail: In the AmberX Android app the rendered page sits too high: the top banner/row is hidden behind the phone's status bar (call notifications) and the camera cutout. Fix edge-to-edge handling: apply system bar and display-cutout insets (WindowInsets / safe-area-inset-top for the web view), so the top row is fully visible. Test on the paired phone, portrait and landscape.

origin.said: Fix the top bar of the AmberX app because it's behind my top banner where my call notifications are. It renders the web page too high up for the screen. The top row is hidden. The banner's behind stuff like my camera.

steps.text: Locate the AmberX Android WebView host (activity/fragment, theme, manifest) and the web shell's top-banner CSS; note current edge-to-edge setup (enableEdgeToEdge / setDecorFitsSystemWindows, windowLayoutInDisplayCutoutMode, viewport meta) and record findings in the build notes.

Native fix: in the WebView host, apply ViewCompat.setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener combining WindowInsetsCompat.Type.systemBars() | displayCutout(); pad the WebView container top/left/right/bottom by those insets (portrait and landscape), set layoutInDisplayCutoutMode to shortEdges, and keep status bar icons readable over the banner colour.

builds.title: Dispatcher: a worktree store write can erase a fresh launch record (double launch, then a stuck build)
builds.detail: Seen on pass-approval-hook-deep-link-amberx-notification, Nov 10 2026 (journal _claude/builds/journal/2026-11-p4.jsonl): 18:11:16 pipeline:launch wrote status running + pipeline.session earl; 18:11:19 the worktree's orchestrator:note ('Claude account: ...', written by claude-headless.sh at start from a store copy taken before the launch) landed with status queued and no pipeline record, and the per-build newer-wins merge kept it; 18:12:11 the next tick launched the same build again (gina), both runs numbered 1. Earl's 's1 done' tick at 18:24:48 erased the second record the same way, so the live build sat in 'running' with no session: checkEnds and reapBuilds both skip a build without pipeline.session / pipeline.account, so the phase end was never handled (set to queued by hand). Fix, in this order: (1) builds-merge-core: merge the pipeline record per field, never let an incoming copy with no pipeline record replace a newer launch record on main (or have orchestrator.mjs act pull main's record before a note/tick write); (2) pipeline-core plan(): never launch a build whose status is running/waiting or that has a running or queued agent slot for its id (agent-slots status lists build per slot); (3) checkEnds/reapBuilds: a build 'running' with no pipeline record and no live slot for it ends by the phase rule (exit 0 + model switch -> queued) instead of being skipped forever; (4) claude-headless.sh: write the 'Claude account' note only after the launch record is published, or through the per-field merge. Add a check in framework/spec/check-builds-live.mjs that replays this journal sequence.

builds.title: Molly gap: axHub allows Molly's origin on /auth/api/* (CORS with credentials) so native screens read the hub session
builds.detail: Found by molly-sign-in-once s1. From https://molly.amberxai.com, GET https://axhub.amberxai.com/auth/api/session answers 200 with no Access-Control-Allow-Origin, and the preflight OPTIONS /auth/api/logout answers 200 with no CORS headers, so a browser on Molly cannot read the hub session or post a write. The hub should answer an allow-list of amberxai.com app origins (Molly first) on /auth/api/* with Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoing the origin, Access-Control-Allow-Credentials true, Access-Control-Allow-Headers content-type, accept, x-axhub-csrf, Vary Origin; never * with credentials. The session cookie is same-site (SameSite=Lax is enough). Molly side is in place: apps/molly/src/molly/credentials.ts (axhub provider, credentials include, X-AxHub-CSRF on writes).

builds.title: Drag anything by API and voice (follow-up to full API control, start only after PR #556 lands): every draggable thing (banner widgets, toolbar items, tabs, dock panes, grid columns/rows, list items, layout slots) gets a move command with drop zones, incl. add/remove/reorder banner widgets; REST, MCP

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

origin.said: I want to be able to drag anything on any page, anything that's draggable, I want to be able to drag it. The regular API build land first.

steps.text: Design the drag-move@1 contract: one shape for every draggable kind (banner-widget, toolbar-item, tab, dock-pane, grid-column, grid-row, list-item, layout-slot), with source id, target container, drop zone (before/after/into/side), index and add/remove. Write the spec in framework/spec/DRAG-MOVE.md and an asset-types/schema entry if one is needed.
steps.why: New cross-app contract for how every GUI's drag targets are addressed

steps.text: Write the reference engine framework/core/engines/drag-move.ts: validate a move, resolve drop zones, compute the new order (pure, no DOM), and add an open registry of draggable kinds that hosts register into.
steps.why: Engine internals that every app's drag hosts share

steps.text: Add golden fixtures framework/spec/fixtures/drag-move.json covering reorder, cross-container move, add, remove, invalid zone and out-of-range index. Generate them with gen-fixtures.mts, record the deferred Kotlin twin in PORTING.md, and add npx tsx framework/spec/check-drag-move.mts.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the cross-port contract

steps.text: Add the runtime seam in framework/react: a useDraggableHost(kind, containerId, {list, apply}) hook that registers a host with the runtime (rt.drag.hosts) so a move can run without a pointer, and give the existing drag code paths a shared apply.
steps.why: Changes how drag works in GUIs across every app

steps.text: Wire banner widgets into the drag host: reorder, move between banner slots, and add/remove a widget through the banner widget host engine, so it is the same code path as a manual drag.
Wire toolbar items (Toolbars plugin toolbars) into the drag host: reorder, move to another toolbar, and add or remove an item or a dropped hook.
Wire TabGroup tabs into the drag host: reorder, plus move to another group where the host allows it. Also cover the hand-drawn strips that carry data-axf-tab-group (Terminal, workspace panes).
Wire dock panes and layout slots into the drag host: move a pane to a side or into a tab stack, and swap or move layout slots, all through the layout engine.
Wire DataGrid columns and rows into the drag host (column reorder, row reorder where the grid allows it) and give generic sortable lists the same hookup.

Sweep the console and apps for other draggable things (Build manager queue rows, Plan Studio, Pipeline, asset library, banner pop-out) and register each one as a host. List anything left over in the report.

Add the console actions drag.list (hosts and items on the current page), drag.zones (drop zones for an item) and drag.move / drag.add / drag.remove, registered with the full-API action registry from PR #556.

Add REST routes: GET /api/drag/hosts, GET /api/drag/zones, and POST /api/drag/move|add|remove, relayed to the open console through the existing remote-command channel. Add a Python validator that matches the engine.

Add MCP tools to mcp_server.py: console_drag_list, console_drag_zones, console_drag_move, console_drag_add and console_drag_remove. Each move is a veto call with a reason, and the read tools are read-only.
Add the CLI command axf drag list|zones|move|add|remove (node framework/cli/drag.mjs) on the same REST routes, with help text in the header comment.
Add voice/AmberX intents ("move the clock widget to the left of the banner", "drag the Logs tab first", "remove the CPU widget"). Each resolves names to ids through drag.list, then calls drag.move.
Add deep links: console_show / console_open targets like drag:<kind>:<host>:<item>, which open the page and highlight the item and its drop zones, plus a state read of the current order per host.
Draw drop zones with tokens only when a move is previewed by API (Follow Amber highlight). Make sure check-theme, check-controls and check-chrome-assets pass.
Add tests: a vitest/tsx test for each host kind that shows an API move gives the same result as a simulated pointer drag, plus server route tests and MCP tool tests.

Add a Playwright smoke test on the built console that runs drag.move on a banner widget, a tab and a grid column through REST, checks the order changed and survives a reload. Wrap it in agent-slots heavy.
Add glossary and help entries for the drag commands and the drag-move contract, update catalog/status.json and tracker.json, and record the API reach for each host in the help docs.

Final step: run the full checks (validate, fixtures, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, tests). Write _claude/builds/reports/drag-anything-by-api-and-voice-follow-up-to-full.md, add the THREADS.md row, and open the PR, listing how each draggable is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

builds.title: Server watchdog: orchestrator auto-recovers stuck or killed builds

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

origin.said: Brett: if anything stops working, the server/orchestrator fixes it automatically with no one asking. Detect builds marked running with no live session (e.g. killed exit 143, failed exit 1), reset and requeue them, retry failed sessions, keep every slot filled, and send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Never wait for Brett to notice.

steps.text: Design the watchdog@1 contract in framework/core/build-watchdog.mjs. A build counts as stuck when it is marked running or queued-running and has no live session: the pid is gone, the tmux session is missing, the heartbeat (lastSeenAt) is older than staleMin, or an exit code is recorded (143 killed, 137 OOM, 1 failed, usage limit). For each case, define the action: reset the running step, release the slot, requeue, retry on the same or another account, or give up after maxRetries and go back to Pending with a banner item. Also define the recovery record shape { at, buildId, phase, step, cause, exit, action, attempt, account, notified }.
steps.why: New cross-app contract that decides builds@1 status transitions

steps.text: Add the JSON schema framework/schemas/build-watchdog.json and register recovery records on builds@1. This adds an optional `recoveries[]` on a build, which normBuild must keep, plus the journal kind `watchdog-recover`. Old records with no recoveries load unchanged, so no migration is needed. Show this in builds-store verify.
steps.why: Schema + store field design on the one builds store

steps.text: Add golden fixtures for the decision table (killed 143, exit 1, stale heartbeat, live session left alone, retry cap reached, usage limit moves to another account) and a check script. Wire the check into CI.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the new contract

steps.text: Have deploy/claude-headless.sh record each run's end: exit code, signal, account and the time it ended. It writes them to the build's run record through builds-live.mjs (and a run-status file under the slot dir), so killed (143) and failed (1) runs leave evidence the watchdog can read.
Add the liveness probe: framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs `alive <build>` checks pid, tmux session and slot heartbeat and returns JSON. Also free slots whose process is gone (orphan slot reaping).

Add watchdog.mjs `scan` (dry run) to the build-orchestrator plugin. It reads the store, finds every running build, probes liveness, applies the build-watchdog.mjs decisions and prints the stuck builds with cause and planned action (--json).

Add watchdog.mjs `run`, which applies the recoveries. It resets the stuck step to pending, releases the slot, sets the build back to queued through pipeline.mjs, appends a recoveries[] entry under the store lock and pushes it live with builds-live.mjs. It does this idempotently, using a per-build lock and a cooldown.

Retry failed sessions. Crashes and kills are retried up to maxRetries (default 3). A usage limit or account error retries on the next worker through deploy/claude-workers.mjs route. When the cap is hit, the build goes to Pending with a note. The retry count lives on the build, not in memory.

Keep every slot filled. After each recovery, and on every watchdog pass, call pipeline.mjs tick while free slots plus Queue work remain. If slots sit idle while the Queue is non-empty, record that as a recovery cause ('idle-slots') and fix it.

Schedule it: add an `axf-watchdog` cron every minute (with flock) to the plugin's install.mjs and remove it in uninstall.mjs. Mount and add the env in the deploy install script. Make the plugin-lifecycle check pass.

Send a phone FYI for every fix. Declare notify type `watchdog.fix` (FYI, low priority) and `watchdog.gave-up` (alert) in notify.json, and send each through axf.notify@1 to the AmberX app with build, cause, action and attempt. Set `notified` on the recovery record and batch several fixes in one pass into one push.

Add the health@1 check 'Build watchdog' in systems-check. It goes red when the last pass is older than 3 minutes or a build gave up. Its auto-fix reinstalls the cron and runs one pass. A gave-up build becomes a banner item with Fix (requeue).

Add Watchdog settings as a section of Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator (level toolbar applies): on/off, interval, stale heartbeat minutes, max retries, retry on another account, FYI per fix or batched. Stored as plugin settings keys that watchdog.mjs reads.

Add a Watchdog panel in Build orchestrator, built from framework controls and tokens only, in a TabGroup tab. It shows last pass, running builds with liveness, recent fixes (cause → action, attempt, notified) and a Run now toolbar (role=toolbar, aria-label). Each build view shows its recoveries list.
Add the REST API: GET watchdog/status, GET watchdog/scan, POST watchdog/run, GET/PUT watchdog/settings, GET builds/<id>/recoveries on the build-orchestrator server routes.

Add the same API on MCP, the CLI and voice: plugin-commands for the routes (watchdog_status/scan/run/settings), CLI `axf watchdog status|scan|run|set`, the voice/console actions `watchdog.run` and `watchdog.status`, and a console_show / console_open deep link target `build-orchestrator/watchdog` (plus `?build=<id>`).

Write unit tests for watchdog.mjs against a temp store (AXF_DATA_DIR): killed 143 is requeued, exit 1 is retried, a stale heartbeat is reset, a live build is untouched, the cap sends the build to Pending, a usage limit goes to the next account, idle slots trigger a tick, one FYI per fix, and a second pass does nothing.

Add an end-to-end test with a fake claude in HOME/.local/bin: launch it through claude-headless.sh, kill it (SIGTERM, 143), run watchdog run, then assert the build was requeued, the slot freed and refilled, the recovery recorded and the notify sent. Run the notify-control registry test.

Write docs and the catalog: a Watchdog section in the plugin README, help entries, plugin.json/command/CLI-header descriptions for the glossary, and the _claude/builds/README.md recovery flow. Run glossary-index catalog.mjs --check, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars and check-chrome-assets.

Submit the Watchdog panel to UI Review with 3 options (layout variants as assets under plugins/build-orchestrator/assets/), each with desktop and phone shots, in group 'server-watchdog-orchestrator-auto-recovers-stuck - <date>'.

- Any picked asset must have a manifest and pass schema conformance before applying.
- Reachable by REST/MCP/CLI/voice/control@1. Tests, help entries, Shipped features.
Works together with the 'all settings interfaces open in a floating dialog' and per-instance settings-window picker builds.

builds.title: Transparency token works on every dialog and settings window
builds.detail:
Root cause: --fx-opacity-glass / opacityGlass only applies where a component's customization has glass:true (framework/core/engines/customize.ts case 'glass'). Settings dialogs and most panels never set it, so the transparency token does nothing there.
Fix: every dialog, settings interface, panel, popover and floating surface uses a token-driven glass background by default (surface mixed with opacityGlass + blur). Add per-surface-type tokens (glass on/off and opacity per surface type: dialog, settings, panel, menu, toolbar, banner) in tokens.style, editable in Token Control and per instance in Quick settings. Rule: everything visual is driven by a token; add a check that fails on hard-coded backgrounds/opacity. Follows skins. Tests, Shipped features.

To make a surface see-through you lower its value. Per surface type tokens in tokens.style, overridable per instance (Quick settings).

builds.title: Console Android app: thin WebView wrapper with overlay, replaces AmberX
builds.detail:
New Android app that replaces AmberX: a thin native shell that runs the AXF console web app in a WebView. Not a native rewrite.
- Native only where Android requires it: draw-over-apps floating toolbar/bubble (port from overlay-toolbar-v2), approvals bar, notifications, mic/recorder, open_url, wake, permissions. Everything else is the web console.
- SAFE AREA (Brett's screenshots, Nov 13): AmberX drew its top bar under the status bar, so the clock, camera cutout, call pill, notification icons and signal sat on top of the title/search/menu. The wrapper must handle WindowInsets (status bar, display cutout, navigation bar, IME), pass them into the WebView as CSS env(safe-area-inset-*) with viewport-fit=cover, and the console must pad every top bar, banner, toolbar and bottom nav with them. Nothing is ever drawn under the clock, camera or notification shade. Test on cutout and punch-hole phones, portrait and landscape.
- The floating toolbar expands to the full-screen console with the toolbar top-left, keeps the app in front, and pops up approvals with a link to the approvals page.
- A JS bridge exposes the native features to the console (window.axfNative), with full API parity: REST/MCP/CLI/voice.
- Auto-updates the web content from the live console. The shell rarely needs a rebuild.
- Migrate AmberX's axHub device service (amberx.open_url, recorder) to the new app.

builds.title: Console app: wake-word voice listener, voice approvals, every console command by voice
builds.detail:
Voice control for the console Android app (wrapper, parts 1-4), working offline where possible.
- Always-on wake-word listener, with a wake phrase Brett sets in Settings (several allowed). Runs on-device (offline engine, e.g. Vosk/whisper.cpp + a local intent matcher), with a mic-on indicator and an off switch.
- After the wake phrase the app answers out loud ('What's up?') and listens for a command.
- Voice approvals: 'approve' reads pending approvals one at a time (who asked, what it does); Brett says approve, deny, skip or details. 'Approve all pending' and 'deny all' ask for one spoken confirm. Works from the floating overlay and the lock screen.
- Settings by voice, e.g. 'change the veto timer to two hours' (the axHub veto countdown, so he has that long to veto something before it runs/builds), with the value read back.
- Command catalog: every console action, plugin command, control@1 target and pipeline gets a voice entry, built from the API registry so new plugins appear automatically. Multi-field actions run as a spoken wizard that asks for each missing field ('create a new project' -> 'name?' -> 'Gizmo Johnson' -> confirm). Covers projects, builds/pipelines (file, split, prioritise, land, stop), approvals, settings, tokens/skins, notes/tasks, navigation.
- A Voice commands screen lists every command and its phrasings, searchable, with custom phrases Brett adds.
- Destructive commands always need a spoken confirm.
- Full API parity. Tests, help, Shipped features.

Follow-up to console-skin-axhub-only (the 'Get my skin only from axHub' switch in Settings > Appearance).
- Under that switch add an 'Override' switch, off by default. The two are mutually exclusive: turning Override on turns 'Inherit from axHub only' off right away, and turning axHub-only back on turns Override off.
- While axHub-only is on and Override is off, nothing about the skin or its assets can be edited anywhere: every screen, panel, inline editor, UI Manager row and property/token field that would change the skin or an asset is greyed out (disabled, not hidden).

- Full API: REST/MCP/CLI/voice/control@1. Tests, help, Shipped features.
